rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate SAP frames with port numbers outside the range 1024–65535 for bi-directional communication.
rules.source_quote: SAP AFDX Ù AFDX AFDX ÙCompliant network 1 024 – 65 535 Used for bi-directional communication: specific TFTP etc..,

rules.name: End System wire-speed throughput capability
rules.consensus_value: End System should handle back-to-back frames (100% wire speed).
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Section 5.1 Performances on page 80 clearly defines that 'The maximum throughput ("wire speed") corresponds to back-to-back frames.' The specification also describes testing this capability using '1 ms burst of back-to-back frames' to measure performance. While the rule refers to End Systems, the specification text confirms this concept applies to system performance measurement.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate continuous back-to-back frames to test if the End System processes them at wire speed.
rules.source_quote: The maximum throughput ('wire speed') corresponds to back-to-back frames.

rules.name: End System invariant parameters for performance
consensus_value: Size of IP multicast group per VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The extracted list of invariant parameters exactly matches what is provided in section 5.1 on page 80-81, including the categorization into Volume (transmission/reception) and Speed (transmission/reception) parameters.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic violating these parameters (e.g., unsupported frame sizes or frame rates) to test End System compliance.
rules.source_quote: As a guide, the following invariant parameters should be provided: Volume in transmission and reception given by: Number of ports, Number of VLs, Number of SubVL, Frame size, Size of IP multicast group per VL. Speed in transmission given by: Latency, Frame rate. Speed in reception given by: Latency, Traffic profile.

rules.name: Port Number Allocation Range
rules.justification: The rule correctly identifies that port numbers range from 0-65535. The specification clearly shows in Figure 3-41 that port allocation covers the full range from 0 to 65,535, divided into different allocation categories. This represents the complete valid range for UDP/TCP port numbers in AFDX systems.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use port numbers outside the specified range and observe if the network rejects them.
rules.source_quote: Port range (decimal value) Allocation range ARINC 664 Allocation range AFDX 0 – 1023 Administered by ICANN 'Well-known' port number Administered by ICANN 'Well-known' port number 1 024 – 16 383 Registered by ICANN A664 assigned 16 384 – 32 767 Registered by ICANN System integrator Or User defined 32 768 – 65 535 Registered by ICANN Recommended for temporary port assignment Assigned by network manager

rules.name: Port Number Uniqueness within a Virtual Link
rules.consensus_value: Two identical port numbers cannot be used within a Virtual Link.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that within a Virtual Link, two identical port numbers cannot be used, which is exactly what the extracted rule states.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use duplicate port numbers within a single Virtual Link and observe if the network rejects them.
rules.source_quote: Port number duplication: the only technical limitation regarding port number duplication is that two identical port number cannot be used with in a Virtual Link.

rules.name: Performance measurement burst duration
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly mentions that performance is measured by the time necessary to process all frames received during a 1 ms burst of back-to-back frames, and this is illustrated in Figure 5-1. The 1 ms duration is clearly specified as the measurement period.
rules.test_hint: Send burst of frames for exactly 1 ms duration and measure if end system can process all frames within specification
rules.source_quote: The actual performance is measured by the time necessary to process all frames received during a 1 ms burst of back-to-back frames

rules.name: Redundancy management disabled during performance test
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The quote 'The redundancy management algorithm is disabled' directly appears in section 5.1 Performances, and the context clearly indicates this is a requirement for performance testing scenarios.
rules.test_hint: During performance testing, verify that redundancy management is not active and both A and B network data are processed as separate VLs
rules.source_quote: The redundancy management algorithm is disabled.

rules.name: Independent end-to-end links
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes the independence of end-to-end links as a key characteristic of the deterministic network architecture, stating that faults in one end system will not affect other fault-free end systems' ability to communicate.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a fault in one end system and observe if other end systems continue to communicate without disruption.
rules.source_quote: a fault in one end system will not affect the ability of fault free end systems to communicate

rules.name: Ethernet Frame Compliance
rules.consensus_value: Frames must comply with IEEE 802.3 standard
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'Any Ethernet Frame generated by the End System should be compliant with IEEE 802.3 standard.' This is a direct behavioral requirement for frame generation compliance.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that do not comply with IEEE 802.3 to test compliance enforcement.
rules.source_quote: Any Ethernet Frame generated by the End System should be compliant with IEEE 802.3 standard.

rules.name: Maximum frame size (Lmax) per VL
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Transmission Flow Control Mechanism
rules.consensus_value: On the transmitting side, the End System function of the switch must construct Ethernet frames and perform the flow control mechanism using the EndSystem_Configuration_Table.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 4.7.3.1 explicitly describes the EndSystem_Configuration_Table's purpose, stating that 'On the transmitting side, construct the Ethernet frames and perform the flow control mechanism.' The rule accurately captures this behavioral requirement for the End System function of the switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that violate flow control parameters (e.g., exceeding BAG or smax) and observe if the switch enforces flow control (e.g., delays or discards frames).
rules.source_quote: On the transmitting side, construct the Ethernet frames and perform the flow control mechanism.

rules.name: Frame discard on link failure
rules.consensus_value: discard_buffered_frames_on_link_failure
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that frames held in buffers of a failed port should be discarded for that port.
rules.test_hint: Simulate link failure on output port and verify buffered frames are discarded
rules.source_quote: In the case of a link failure of a port, frames forwarded to and held in buffers of this port should be discarded for this port.

rules.name: Frame size compliance with VL maximum
rules.consensus_value: Ethernet frame size (L) must be less than or equal to Lmax for the VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. In the filtering function section, it clearly lists 'Ethernet frame size (L) less that or equal to Lmax' as one of the aspects tested during frame filtering. This is a legitimate frame size constraint that must be enforced by switches.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with L > Lmax for a given VL.
rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) less that or equal to Lmax

rules.name: Frame size compliance with VL minimum (byte-based policing)
rules.consensus_value: Ethernet frame size (S) must be greater than or equal to Smin for the VL when byte-based traffic policing is used
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement for Ethernet frame size (S) to be greater than or equal to Smin when byte-based traffic policing is used is clearly listed as one of the filtering function tests performed by the switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with S < Smin for a VL configured with byte-based policing.
rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (S) greater than or equal to Smin, only in case where byte-based traffic policing is used

rules.name: No Unused Bytes Between Data Primitives
rules.consensus_value: Data primitives must be placed consecutively with no unused bytes between them, except for padding for alignment purposes.
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text explicitly states that 'Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.' This directly supports the behavioral constraint that data primitives must be placed consecutively with no unused bytes between them, except for padding for alignment purposes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can insert arbitrary unused bytes between data primitives in a data set and observe if the receiver misinterprets or discards the frame.
rules.source_quote: Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.

rules.name: Spare Fields Must Be Zero-Filled
rules.consensus_value: Spare data fields must be filled with binary zeros if unused.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.' This is a behavioral requirement that spare fields must contain binary zeros when not used for actual data.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate spare fields with non-zero values (e.g., 0xFF, 0xAA, random bytes) and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.
rules.source_quote: Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.

rules.name: Reserved Field Must Be Zero-Filled
rules.consensus_value: The 32-bit reserved field must be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that the 32-bit reserved field at the beginning of the global message structure should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate the reserved field with non-zero values (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x55555555) and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.
rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: Global Spare Field Must Be Zero-Filled
rules.consensus_value: The global spare field must be filled with all binary zeros if included in a message.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that the Global Spare field, when included in a message, should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate the global spare field with non-zero values and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.
rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: No Shifting of Data Set Positions
rules.consensus_value: Modifications to a message must not shift the position of existing data sets within the message.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 1-3.6 'Guidelines for Designing Messages'. The specification clearly states that when modifying existing message structures, modifications should be done 'in a manner that does not shift the position of the data sets in the message.' This is a behavioral constraint on message modification to minimize cost of change.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where data sets are reordered or shifted (e.g., inserting bytes before an existing data set) and observe if the receiver misinterprets the frame.
rules.source_quote: messages should be modified in a manner that does not shift the position of the data sets in the message.

rules.name: Fragment Transmission Order
rules.consensus_value: fragments_transmitted_in_order
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.' in section 3.3.1.1.2.1 dealing with queuing service transmission. The extracted rule correctly captures this behavioral requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send a fragmented message and verify fragments are transmitted to the network in the correct order
rules.source_quote: When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.

rules.name: Complete reassembly requirement
rules.consensus_value: no data presented to partition until whole message reassembled
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The exact quote from section 3.3.1.1.2.2 confirms that fragmented messages must be completely reassembled before any data is presented to the partition's queuing service FIFO.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented packets and verify partial data is not delivered before all fragments arrive
rules.source_quote: In case of fragmentation, no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until whole message has been reassembled.

rules.name: maximum datagram size to off-network destinations
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document shows RFC 1122 paragraph 3.3.3 requirement that 'In the absence of actual knowledge of the minimum MTU along the path, the IP layer SHOULD use EMTU_S <= 576 whenever the destination address is not on a connected network'. The extracted rule correctly identifies this as a maximum datagram size constraint of 576 bytes for off-network destinations.
rules.test_hint: Send datagrams larger than 576 bytes to off-network destinations to test MTU enforcement
rules.source_quote: In the absence of actual knowledge of the minimum MTU along the path, the IP layer SHOULD use EMTU_S <= 576 whenever the destination address is not on a connected network

rules.name: packet size limited by MTU
rules.consensus_value: packet size must not exceed network MTU, oversized datagrams must be fragmented
rules.justification: The rule accurately reflects the specification's statement about packet size limitations and fragmentation behavior. The specification clearly states that packet size is limited by MTU and that oversized UDP datagrams must be fragmented.
rules.test_hint: Send packets larger than the configured MTU to test fragmentation handling or rejection
rules.source_quote: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU (Max Transfer Unit) of the network. Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.

rules.name: Fixed-length ARINC 429 label encapsulation
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The document explicitly states 'Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive' as the first approach for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting. This establishes that ARINC 429 labels must be encapsulated in exactly 32-bit fixed-length opaque data primitives.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with ARINC 429 labels encapsulated in non-32-bit lengths (e.g., 16-bit or 64-bit).
rules.source_quote: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive

rules.name: Data Set (DS) field usage for multi-label messages
rules.consensus_value: Must reflect the status of the concentrator; single DS for single-threaded devices, multiple DS for fault-tolerant concentrators
rules.justification: This rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text clearly describes how DS (Data Set) fields should be used differently based on the concentrator design: single DS for single-threaded devices, multiple DS for fault-tolerant concentrators where portions could fail independently.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched DS/FS pairs or omit DS fields in multi-label messages.
rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used [...] If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail [...] more than one DS should be considered.

rules.name: Variable-length opaque structure maximum size
rules.consensus_value: Must be statically configured based on the maximum number of labels arriving between transmissions
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a key requirement from the specification. The text explicitly states that 'The system designer must figure out what the highest or maximum number of labels is that could possibly arrive at the gateway between transmissions. From this maximum number the maximum size of the variable length opaque structure is established. This structure is then statically configured into the system.' This directly supports the rule's constraint that the maximum opaque structure size must be statically configured based on the maximum number of labels.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames exceeding the statically configured maximum size for variable-length opaque structures.
rules.source_quote: The system designer must figure out what the highest or maximum number of labels is that could possibly arrive at the gateway between transmissions. From this maximum number the maximum size of the variable length opaque structure is established.

rules.name: Padding of unused opaque structure bytes
rules.consensus_value: Must be filled with binary zeros
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros.' This is a specific behavioral requirement for padding unused bytes in the variable length opaque structure used for ARINC 429 integration.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate unused bytes with non-zero values or random data.
rules.source_quote: The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros.

rules.name: Maximum AFDX Frame Length
rules.consensus_value: Defined per VL
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The quote 'A maximum AFDX frame length should be defined on a per VL basis' appears exactly in section 3.3.3.1 ES MAC Profile. The rule correctly identifies that frame length limits are defined per Virtual Link (VL), which is a fundamental aspect of AFDX traffic management.
rules.test_hint: Send frames exceeding the maximum length defined for a VL to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: A maximum AFDX frame length should be defined on a per VL basis.

rules.name: Unique Message Identification
rules.consensus_value: Each message in the AFDX network is uniquely identified by a quintuplet consisting of UDP Source Port, Source IP, Destination MAC, Destination IP, and UDP Destination Port.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines that peer-to-peer communications are identified by a quintuplet consisting of UDP Source Port + Source IP + Destination MAC (VL identification) + Destination IP + UDP Destination Port, and explicitly states that 'In the AFDX network, this quintuplet provides a unique identification for each message.'
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could attempt to send frames with non-unique quintuplets to test if the network correctly identifies and handles them.
rules.source_quote: In the AFDX network, this quintuplet provides a unique identification for each message.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence Validity
rules.consensus_value: FCS embedded in the frame must match the calculation upon reception
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a frame filtering requirement explicitly stated in the specification. The FCS (Frame Check Sequence) validation is clearly described as one of the frame integrity checks performed by the filtering function.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect FCS to test if they are discarded.
rules.source_quote: The frame integrity: whether the FCS embedded in the frame matches the calculation upon reception

rules.name: Destination Address Validity
rules.consensus_value: Destination Address must correspond to a valid VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The frame filtering section clearly describes that one of the filtering criteria is 'The frame path: whether the destination requested by the content of the Destination Address field (which in case of the AFDX is the Virtual Link Identifier) of the arriving frame is permitted or not'. Additionally, the specification explicitly lists 'Destination address validity (Ethernet Address corresponds to a valid VL, including constant field)' as one of the aspects tested in the filtering function.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid destination addresses to test if they are discarded.
rules.source_quote: The frame path: whether the destination requested by the content of the Destination Address field (which in case of the AFDX is the Virtual Link Identifier) of the arriving frame is permitted or not

rules.name: Frame size envelope validation
rules.consensus_value: Frames must not be longer or shorter than the allowed envelope (Smin ≤ S ≤ Smax or Lmin ≤ L ≤ Lmax)
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The filtering function explicitly checks 'whether the frame is either longer or shorter than the envelope allows'. The specification also defines frame size parameters including Smin, Smax (for Ethernet line size) and Lmin, Lmax (for Ethernet frame size), confirming the envelope concept.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames outside the allowed size envelope for a VL.
rules.source_quote: The frame size: whether the frame is either longer or shorter than the envelope allows

rules.name: Received Frame Consistency Check
rules.consensus_value: On the receiving side, the End System function of the switch must check the consistency of the received frame using the EndSystem_Configuration_Table.
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 4.7.3.1 clearly explains that the End System function of the Switch uses the EndSystem_Configuration_Table and explicitly states that on the receiving side, it should 'check the consistency of the received frame'.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with inconsistencies (e.g., mismatched VL identifiers, incorrect frame sizes, or corrupted headers) and observe if the switch discards them.
rules.source_quote: On the receiving side, check the consistency of the received frame.

rules.name: Valid Functional Status Values
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'If a receiver reads a functional status value other than 0,3,12, or 48, it will discard the data in the associated DS.' Table 1-3 confirms these are the only valid decimal values for functional status enumerations: ND=0, NO=3, FT=12, NCD=48.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can inject frames with functional_status values outside [0, 3, 12, 48] (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 5, 11, 13, 47, 49) and observe if the receiver discards the associated data set.
rules.source_quote: If a receiver reads a functional status value other than 0,3,12, or 48, it will discard the data in the associated DS.

rules.name: Parameter removal padding requirement
rules.consensus_value: Replace removed parameters with pad bytes; do not shift remaining message content.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. It appears as guideline #4 in section 1-3.6 'Guidelines for Designing Messages' which provides clear instructions on how to handle parameter removal.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where parameters are removed without padding or where remaining content is shifted, violating the no-shift rule.
rules.source_quote: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.

rules.name: Parameter insertion in spare/pad fields
rules.consensus_value: Insert new parameters in spare or pad fields to avoid shifting existing message parameters.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Point 5 in the guidelines for designing messages directly states this requirement to minimize impact by avoiding shifts in existing message parameters and inserting new parameters in spare or pad fields.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where new parameters are inserted in non-spare/pad fields, causing shifts in existing parameters.
rules.source_quote: Minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields.

rules.name: Global spare usage for new parameters/data sets
rules.consensus_value: Use global spare to add new parameters to the last data set (if covered by existing FS) or to add a new data set (if represented by a different FS).
rules.justification: The rule correctly captures the specification's guidance on global spare usage. The spec clearly states that global spare 'might have space for a future DS that is part of FDSn or it could contain space for 2 additional DS for FDSn plus another complete FDS', indicating it can add parameters to existing data sets or create new functional data sets. The rule's logic about using functional status (FS) to determine whether to add to existing or create new data sets aligns with the specification's functional data set structure.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where global spare is misused (e.g., adding parameters to a non-last data set or creating a new data set when existing FS applies).
rules.source_quote: Global spare can be used to add a complete new data set to the end of a message, or be used to add parameters to the last data set defined in the message. The choice of which one to do is driven by the functional status. If the new parameter(s) is covered by the existing FS, put them in the last data set. If the new parameter(s) are represented by a different FS, create a new data set.

rules.name: Byte and bit ordering in data primitives
rules.consensus_value: Most significant byte on the left, least significant byte on the right; most significant bit on the left, least significant bit on the right.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly describes the byte and bit ordering convention for data primitives in AFDX message structures.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with reversed byte or bit order in data primitives to test network validation.
rules.source_quote: The boxes that represent a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, the most significant byte on the left, the least significant byte on the right. Also, the bits in the bytes are most significant bit on the left and least significant bit on the right.

rules.name: Data element alignment via padding
rules.consensus_value: Padding maintains alignment of data elements in the message.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavioral requirement stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'The padding in this example maintains the alignment of the data elements' in section 1-4.2, which directly supports the rule that padding maintains alignment of data elements in messages.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with misaligned data elements (e.g., unaligned 32-bit integers) to test network handling.
rules.source_quote: The padding in this example maintains the alignment of the data elements.

rules.name: Transmission of entire static structure
rules.consensus_value: Must transmit the entire statically configured structure, not just the used portion
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes that when using variable length opaque structures for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting, the gateway must transmit the entire statically configured structure, not just the portion containing valid data.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can truncate frames to only include the used portion of the opaque structure.
rules.source_quote: The message is then sent, with the entire static structure, not just the used portion.

rules.name: AFDX_frame_encapsulation_order
rules.justification: The rule correctly describes the AFDX frame encapsulation order as specified in Appendix C. The specification clearly defines the hierarchical structure: Frame (MAC header + packet) -> Packet (IP header + data) -> Message (transport protocol header + application data). This matches the extracted order of MAC header, IP header, UDP/TCP header, Application Data.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect encapsulation order, e.g., swapping IP header and UDP header or omitting the MAC header.
rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet. A packet is the unit of data passed across the interface between the IP layer and the data link layer (MAC). It includes an IP header and data. A message consists of a transport protocol header followed by application data.

rules.name: UDP_datagram_fragmentation_constraint
rules.consensus_value: UDP datagrams exceeding MTU size must be fragmented into packets.
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The source quote accurately reflects the specification's statement about UDP datagram fragmentation when the datagram exceeds MTU size.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate oversized UDP datagrams without fragmentation or with malformed fragments (e.g., overlapping offsets).
rules.source_quote: Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.

rules.name: packet_size_limit_by_MTU
rules.consensus_value: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU of the network.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a fundamental principle stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU (Max Transfer Unit) of the network.' This is a genuine behavioral constraint that affects packet processing and fragmentation in AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate packets exceeding the AFDX MTU (typically 1518 bytes for standard Ethernet frames).
rules.source_quote: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU (Max Transfer Unit) of the network.

rules.name: Single Label Message Structure
rules.consensus_value: A single ARINC 429 label should be placed in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive for single label messages.
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text clearly states in Appendix B that 'Figure B-1.1 is an example of how a single label would be placed in a message. This structure should be used for single label messages.' The specification describes Approach 1 as 'Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive' and shows this in the figure with the A429 Label field.
rules.test_hint: Generate a frame with a single ARINC 429 label not placed in a 32-bit opaque data primitive and observe if the network processes it correctly.
rules.source_quote: Figure B-1.1 is an example of how a single label would be placed in a message. This structure should be used for single label messages.

rules.name: Multiple Label Message Structure with Single DS
rules.consensus_value: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote appears in Appendix B describing guidelines for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting, specifically addressing the behavior when multiple labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device.
rules.test_hint: Create a frame with multiple labels using a single DS and check if the network correctly interprets the FS status.
rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS.

rules.name: Multiple Label Message Structure with Multiple DS
rules.consensus_value: If a concentrator device can fail partially, more than one DS should be considered, with each DS represented by its own FS.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's requirement for using multiple DS when a concentrator device can fail partially. The extracted behavioral constraint correctly reflects the condition and action described in the spec.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a partial failure in a concentrator device and ensure that multiple DS are used with individual FS statuses.
rules.source_quote: If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail in some way that causes some labels to be invalid, but a completely legal Ethernet frame is still generated with some valid labels, more than one DS should be considered.

rules.name: Variable Length Opaque Structure
rules.consensus_value: A variable length opaque structure is used when the number of ARINC 429 labels varies, with the structure's maximum size statically configured.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's description of using variable length opaque structures for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting when the number of labels varies. The specification explicitly states this approach is needed when gateways send messages with varying numbers of labels, and that the maximum size must be statically configured.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with varying numbers of labels without using a variable length structure and check if the network processes it correctly.
rules.source_quote: Since any one message the gateway sends could have a varying number of labels, a variable length data structure is required.

rules.name: Frame filtering based on addresses
rules.consensus_value: filter_by_destination_addresses_and_physical_connections
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the frame filtering behavior described in the specification. The specification clearly states that 'Frame based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. Valid frame being defined by analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.' The rule correctly identifies that filtering is based on multiple address levels and physical connections.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect destination addresses (UDP/TCP port, IP, or MAC) to verify they are filtered out and not forwarded to communication/SAP ports
rules.source_quote: Frame based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. Valid frame being defined by analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.

rules.name: Non-compliant frames must be discarded and MIB updated
rules.consensus_value: discard_frame_and_update_MIB
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes that when frame properties do not comply with configuration parameters, the frame is filtered (i.e., discarded) AND one or more MIB entries are updated. This is a behavioral requirement that combines both the discard action and the MIB update action.
rules.test_hint: Send non-compliant frames and verify they are discarded and MIB counters are incremented
rules.source_quote: If the frame properties do not comply with the configuration parameters, the frame is filtered i.e. discarded, and one or more MIB entries updated

rules.name: Maximum frame size support
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The exact quote 'The End System should accommodate VL frames up to a size of 1518 bytes in both transmission and reception.' directly supports the maximum frame size constraint of 1518 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than 1518 bytes and verify they are rejected or handled appropriately
rules.source_quote: The End System should accommodate VL frames up to a size of 1518 bytes in both transmission and reception.

rules.name: Receiver Demultiplexing Based on Destination Addresses
rules.consensus_value: demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The commentary section clearly states 'At the receiver, the demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address.' This is a precise behavioral specification for how receivers should perform demultiplexing operations.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with same destination addresses but different source addresses to verify receiver only uses destination fields for demultiplexing
rules.source_quote: At the receiver, the demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address.

rules.name: Maximum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines S_i_max as 'the maximum frame size for VLi is denoted S i max (expressed in bytes)' and indicates it is a configurable parameter. While the specific range [84, 1538] is mentioned in the source quote but cut off in the provided text, the parameter itself and its definition as a maximum frame size in bytes is confirmed.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL with frame size outside the configured S_i_max range
rules.source_quote: The maximum frame size for VLi is denoted S i max (expressed in bytes). S i max is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]

rules.name: Minimum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly defines S_i_min as the minimum frame size for VL_i and specifies it should be in the range [84, 1538] bytes.
rules.test_hint: Configure S_i_min outside the valid range or send frames smaller than configured S_i_min
rules.source_quote: The minimum frame size for VLi is denoted S i min (expressed in bytes). S i min is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence preservation
rules.consensus_value: no_modification_allowed
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames' and provides additional context about CRC not being regenerated within the switch under any circumstance, including at re-transmission.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with specific FCS values and verify switch does not regenerate or modify them
rules.source_quote: The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames.

rules.name: CRC regeneration prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'the CRC may not be regenerated within the switch under any circumstance, including at re-transmission.' This is a categorical prohibition, making the boolean constraint value of 'false' for CRC regeneration correct.
rules.test_hint: Force switch to retransmit frames and verify CRC remains unchanged from original
rules.source_quote: the CRC may not be regenerated within the switch under any circumstance, including at re-transmission.

rules.name: frame composition at ethernet level
rules.consensus_value: frame consists of MAC header followed by packet data
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the definition of a frame at Ethernet level as stated in the ARINC 664 Part 7 specification. The extracted value correctly describes the basic composition of an Ethernet frame.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with missing MAC headers, corrupted MAC headers, or incorrect frame structure
rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet.

rules.name: Continuous gateway pinging prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote matches exactly with the text in section 3.3.1.4 which states 'In particular, hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously.' The boolean constraint value of false correctly represents this prohibition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send continuous ICMP echo requests to a gateway.
rules.source_quote: hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously.

rules.name: Conditional pinging requirement
rules.consensus_value: Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows two separate but related requirements in section 3.3.1.4: 'Ping only when traffic being sent' states 'Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway…' and 'Ping only when no positive indication' completes the sentence with '...and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.' Together they form the complete behavioral rule that pinging must only be used under both conditions.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP echo requests when no traffic is being sent or when positive indications of gateway functionality exist.
rules.source_quote: Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway… and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.

rules.name: Silently Discard Unknown ICMP Types
rules.consensus_value: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it must be silently discarded.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement to silently discard ICMP messages with unknown type is clearly documented in section 3.2.2 with the exact wording provided in the rule.
rules.test_hint: Send an ICMP message with an unknown type and check if it is discarded without any response.
rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.

rules.name: ICMP Error Message Content
rules.consensus_value: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote matches exactly with the text found in the specification.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram that triggers an ICMP error and verify the content of the returned ICMP error message.
rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.

rules.name: ICMP Echo Server Requirement
rules.consensus_value: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.' appears in section 3.2.2.6 of the specification.
rules.test_hint: Test by sending an ICMP Echo Request and verifying that an Echo Reply is sent back by the host.
rules.source_quote: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.

rules.name: Pass Echo Reply to Higher Layer
rules.consensus_value: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.' appears in section 3.2.2.6 of the specification.
rules.test_hint: Verify that Echo Replies are correctly passed to the ICMP user interface.
rules.source_quote: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence validation requirement
rules.consensus_value: test_frame_with_CRC_and_discard_if_corrupted
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly requires that switches test each frame using the Frame Check Sequence (CRC) field according to IEEE Std 802.3 and discard frames that do not satisfy this test to guarantee total network robustness.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with corrupted CRC values and verify they are discarded by the switch
rules.source_quote: In order to guarantee total network robustness, it is important that only uncorrupted frames be forwarded. Therefore, upon arrival, the switch should test each frame by use of the Frame Check Sequence (CRC) field according to IEEE Std 802.3. The Switch should discard Frames that do not satisfy this test.

rules.name: Ethernet frame size upper limit
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.' The extracted rule correctly captures the upper limit of ≤ 1518 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than 1518 bytes and verify they are discarded
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.

rules.name: Ethernet frame size lower limit
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.' This confirms both the minimum size requirement (≥ 64 bytes) and that frames less than 64 bytes should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than 64 bytes and verify they are discarded
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.

rules.name: Frame Size Alignment
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The switch must discard frames that are not an integral number of octets, which represents an alignment error. The rule correctly identifies this as a boolean constraint (true means frames must be properly aligned).
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a non-integral number of octets (e.g., fractional bits)
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames having an Ethernet frame size that is not an integral number of octets (alignment errors).

rules.name: Maximum Frame Size Enforcement
rules.consensus_value: frame_size <= VL_Lmax
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The source quote exactly matches the text in section 4.2.1 Frame Filtering, which states that switches should discard frames with total Ethernet line size greater than the maximum size (Lmax) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with size exceeding the configured Lmax for its VL
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is greater than the maximum size (Lmax) allowed for the relevant VL, as such a frame would consume more bandwidth than allocated.

rules.name: Minimum Frame Size Enforcement (Byte-based Policing)
rules.consensus_value: frame_size >= VL_Smin (when byte-based policing enabled)
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote directly matches the text found in section 4.2.1 Frame Filtering, which states that when byte-based policing is used, the switch should discard frames smaller than the minimum size (Smin) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: When byte-based policing is enabled, send a frame smaller than the configured Smin for its VL
rules.source_quote: In the case where byte-based policing is used, the switch should also discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is smaller than the minimum size (Smin) allowed for the relevant VL.

rules.name: MAC Destination Address Constant Field Validation
rules.consensus_value: 32-bit constant field in MAC destination address must be correct
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The switch is required to discard incoming frames with a MAC destination address that has an erroneous 32-bit constant field.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with an incorrect 32-bit constant field in the MAC destination address
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames with a MAC destination address that has an erroneous 32-bit constant field.

rules.name: VL Port Authorization
rules.consensus_value: VL id must be authorized for the incoming port
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that frames with unauthorized VL IDs on a port should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a VL ID that is not configured as allowed on the incoming port
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames for which the VL id is not allowed on the incoming port.

rules.name: Source Route Option Processing in Echo Reply
rules.consensus_value: must_reverse_source_route_for_reply
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'If a Source Route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply message.' appears in section 3.2.2.6 and matches the extracted rule perfectly.
rules.test_hint: Send echo request with source route option and verify the echo reply reverses the route correctly
rules.source_quote: If a Source Route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply message.

rules.name: Silently discard unknown ICMP messages
rules.consensus_value: MUST silently discard ICMP messages of unknown type
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement is clearly documented in section 3.2.2 under Internet Control Message Protocol requirements.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP messages with unknown types and verify they are silently discarded.
rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.

rules.name: ICMP error message content
rules.consensus_value: MUST include Internet header and at least first 8 data octets of triggering datagram; more than 8 octets MAY be sent
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.' This matches exactly what is described in the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger ICMP errors and verify the response includes at least 8 octets of the original datagram.
rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.

rules.name: ICMP error message TOS
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'An ICMP error message SHOULD be sent with normal (i.e., zero) TOS bits.' The extracted rule correctly identifies this as requiring TOS value of 0 for ICMP error messages.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP error messages with non-zero TOS bits and verify they are corrected or rejected.
rules.source_quote: An ICMP error message SHOULD be sent with normal (i.e., zero) TOS bits.

rules.name: Validation of ICMP Redirect message gateway address
rules.consensus_value: The new gateway address must be on the same connected (sub-)net through which the Redirect arrived, and the source of the Redirect must be the current first-hop gateway for the specified destination.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the validation requirements for ICMP Redirect message gateway addresses as specified in RFC 1122 Paragraph 3.2.2.2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Redirect messages with invalid gateway addresses (e.g., off-subnet or from a non-first-hop gateway) and verify they are discarded by the receiving End System.
rules.source_quote: A Redirect message SHOULD be silently discarded if the new gateway address it specifies is not on the same connected (sub-) net through which the Redirect arrived, or if the source of the Redirect is not the current first-hop gateway for the specified destination.

rules.name: Conditional transmission of ICMP Source Quench messages
rules.consensus_value: A host MAY send a Source Quench message if it is approaching or has reached the point of discarding datagrams due to buffer or resource shortages.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote matches exactly with the specification text found on page 120, and the extracted behavioral constraint accurately captures the MAY requirement for sending Source Quench messages under specific buffer/resource shortage conditions.
rules.source_quote: A host MAY send a Source Quench message if it is approaching, or has reached, the point at which it is forced to discard incoming datagrams due to a shortage of reassembly buffers or other resources.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Time Exceeded processing in AFDX
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The comment 'Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.' appears multiple times in the ICMP handling section, indicating that all other ICMP message types (including Time Exceeded) are prohibited in AFDX. This directly supports the rule that ICMP Time Exceeded processing should be false/disabled.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Time Exceeded messages and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Destination Unreachable processing in AFDX
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification clearly states 'No ICMP errors' in multiple places throughout the ICMP handling section, including specifically for ICMP Destination Unreachable processing. The table shows 'X' marks under 'MUST NOT' column with 'No ICMP errors' comments, indicating that AFDX End Systems must not process ICMP error messages, including Destination Unreachable messages.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Destination Unreachable messages (codes 0, 1, 2, 3, 5) and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.
rules.source_quote: No ICMP errors

rules.name: Interpretation of transient ICMP Destination Unreachable codes
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately extracted. The specification clearly states that ICMP Destination Unreachable messages with codes 0 (Net), 1 (Host), or 5 (Bad Source Route) may result from routing transients and MUST be interpreted as only hints. The extracted values [0, 1, 5] correctly represent these specific codes.
rules.source_quote: A Destination Unreachable message that is received with code 0 (Net), 1 (Host), or 5 (Bad Source Route) may result from a routing transient and MUST therefore be interpreted as only a hint.

rules.name: Mandatory ICMP Echo server function
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly shows under 'ICMP Echo Request or Reply' section that 'Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.' This is marked with an 'X' under the 'MUST' column, indicating it is a mandatory requirement.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Echo Requests to an End System and verify if it responds with an Echo Reply. Absence of a reply violates this rule.
rules.source_quote: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.

rules.name: Silently discard Echo Request to broadcast or multicast address
rules.consensus_value: MAY silently discard
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement that 'An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded' is clearly documented in section 3.2.2.6 of RFC 1122. The extracted rule accurately captures both the behavioral nature (MAY silently discard) and the condition (destination to broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Echo Requests to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify if they are silently discarded (no reply or error message).
rules.source_quote: An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.

rules.name: Echo Reply must include all data from Echo Request
rules.consensus_value: MUST entirely include the data received in the ICMP Echo Request
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The requirement that data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply is clearly documented in section 3.2.2.6.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with specific data payload and verify if the Echo Reply contains the exact same payload. Truncation or modification violates this rule.
rules.source_quote: Data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply.

rules.name: Pass Echo Reply to ICMP user interface
rules.consensus_value: MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface unless the Echo Request originated in the IP layer
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The behavioral requirement that Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface (with the exception when the Echo Request originated in the IP layer) is clearly documented in the table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request from an application layer and verify if the Echo Reply is delivered to the application. Failure to deliver violates this rule.
rules.source_quote: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.

rules.name: Reflect Record Route and Time Stamp options in Echo Reply
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD update and include Record Route and/or Time Stamp options without truncation
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact requirement is found in section 3.2.2.6 regarding ICMP Echo Request/Reply handling, specifically about reflecting Record Route and Time Stamp options.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with Record Route or Time Stamp options and verify if the Echo Reply includes the updated options without truncation. Missing or truncated options violate this rule.
rules.source_quote: If a Record Route and/or Time Stamp option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, this option (these options) SHOULD be updated to include the current host and included in the IP header of the Echo Reply message, without "truncation".

rules.name: Reverse and reflect Source Route option in Echo Reply
rules.consensus_value: MUST reverse the return route and use it as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact requirement is found in section 3.2.2.6 regarding ICMP Echo Request/Reply handling, specifically for Source Route options.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with a Source Route option and verify if the Echo Reply uses the reversed route. Incorrect or missing reversed route violates this rule.
rules.source_quote: If a Source Route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply message.

rules.name: Prohibit ICMP Information Request or Reply messages
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'A host SHOULD NOT implement these messages' in reference to ICMP Information Request or Reply messages (section 3.2.2.7). The specification consistently indicates that only ICMP echo request and echo reply are allowed, and Information Request/Reply messages are prohibited.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Information Request or Reply messages and verify if they are discarded or rejected by the network.
rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD NOT implement these messages.

rules.name: Silently discard Timestamp Request to broadcast or multicast address
rules.consensus_value: MAY silently discard
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'An ICMP Timestamp Request message to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded' appears in the specification, confirming both the behavioral constraint (MAY silently discard) and the conditions (timestamp request to broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Timestamp Requests to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify if they are silently discarded (no reply or error message).
rules.source_quote: An ICMP Timestamp Request message to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.

rules.name: Timestamp Reply source address must match Timestamp Request destination address
rules.consensus_value: MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding Timestamp Request
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches what is written in the spec under section 3.2.2.8 regarding ICMP Timestamp Reply source address requirements.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Timestamp Request with a specific destination address and verify if the Timestamp Reply's source address matches it. Mismatch violates this rule.
rules.source_quote: The IP source address in an ICMP Timestamp Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding Timestamp Request message.

rules.name: Timestamp value format
rules.consensus_value: milliseconds since midnight Universal Time
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'The preferred form for a timestamp value (the "standard value") is in units of milliseconds since midnight Universal Time.' is found in section 3.2.2.8, which matches the rule's description of timestamp value format requirements.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Timestamp messages with malformed timestamp values (e.g., negative values, values exceeding 86400000 ms) and observe network reaction.
rules.source_quote: The preferred form for a timestamp value (the "standard value") is in units of milliseconds since midnight Universal Time.

rules.name: Address Mask source configurability
rules.consensus_value: MUST be configurable
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'The choice of method to be used in a particular host MUST be configurable...' in section 3.2.2.9 regarding ICMP Address Mask Request and Reply. The extracted rule correctly identifies this as a behavioral requirement for configurability.
rules.source_quote: The choice of method to be used in a particular host MUST be configurable…

rules.name: Static address mask support
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Support static configuration of address mask 3.2.2.9' as a requirement, indicating that static address mask configuration must be supported.
rules.source_quote: Support static configuration of address mask

rules.name: Default address mask assumption
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD assume mask appropriate for the address class of the IP address
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'When method 3, until it has received an Address Mask Reply, the host SHOULD assume a mask appropriate for the address class of the IP address.' This matches the extracted rule's behavioral constraint and value exactly.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can delay or block Address Mask Replies and verify if the AFDX End System falls back to a default mask based on IP address class.
rules.source_quote: When method 3, until it has received an Address Mask Reply, the host SHOULD assume a mask appropriate for the address class of the IP address.

rules.name: First Address Mask Reply usage
rules.consensus_value: MUST use the first Address Mask Reply received to set the address mask
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that when using method 3 (ICMP Address Mask Request/Reply), the first Address Mask Reply message received MUST be used to set the address mask corresponding to the particular local IP address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send multiple Address Mask Replies with conflicting masks and observe if the AFDX End System uses only the first one received.
rules.source_quote: When method 3, the first Address Mask Reply message received MUST be used to set the address mask corresponding to the particular local IP address.

rules.name: Address Mask reasonableness check
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD make some reasonableness check on any address mask it installs
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'A host SHOULD make some reasonableness check on any address mask it installs' in section 3.2.2.9, which matches exactly with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send Address Mask Replies with unreasonable masks (e.g., 0.0.0.0, 255.255.255.255, or masks not aligned with IP address class) and observe if the AFDX End System rejects them.
rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD make some reasonableness check on any address mask it installs.

rules.name: Authoritative agent configuration requirement
rules.consensus_value: MUST be explicitly configured as an address mask agent
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the specification requirement that authoritative agents must be explicitly configured as address mask agents.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an Address Mask Request to an AFDX End System not explicitly configured as an agent and observe if it responds with a Reply.
rules.source_quote: An authoritative agent may be a host or a gateway, but it MUST be explicitly configured as a address mask agent.

rules.name: Static configuration authorization flag
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD have an additional configuration flag for authoritative agent status
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote matches exactly with the text found in section 3.2.2.9, and the behavioral constraint accurately captures the SHOULD requirement for an additional configuration flag.
rules.source_quote: With a statically configured address mask, there SHOULD be an additional configuration flag that determines whether the host is to act as an authoritative agent for this mask.

rules.name: Fault indicator state during INIT mode
rules.consensus_value: fault indicator must stay in fault state during INIT mode
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state.' appears in section 4.8.2.1 Initialization Sequence.
rules.test_hint: Monitor fault indicator during switch initialization to verify it remains in fault state throughout INIT mode
rules.source_quote: During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state.

rules.name: Unknown ICMP Type Handling
rules.consensus_value: silently_discard_unknown_types
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Silently discard ICMP messages with unknown type 3.2.2 X' in the requirements table, followed by the exact quote 'If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.' This confirms both the behavioral requirement and the mandatory nature of silently discarding unknown ICMP types.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages with undefined or reserved type values to verify they are silently discarded
rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.

rules.name: ICMP Error Payload Minimum
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The text clearly states 'Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.' The constraint '≥8 octets' accurately captures the 'at least the first 8 data octets' requirement.
rules.test_hint: Generate conditions that trigger ICMP errors and verify the error message contains at least 8 octets of original datagram data
rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.

rules.name: ICMP Error Message Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification consistently states 'No ICMP errors' in multiple contexts throughout the ICMP section, indicating that ICMP error message generation is prohibited in AFDX. This appears in multiple requirement entries where ICMP error functionality is marked as 'MUST NOT' with the comment 'No ICMP errors'.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to trigger ICMP error generation (invalid IP headers, unreachable destinations, etc.) and verify no ICMP error messages are sent
rules.source_quote: No ICMP errors

rules.name: ICMP Redirect Prohibition from End Systems
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows 'Host send Redirect 3.2.2.2 X No ICMP redirect from ES' with the comment 'A host SHOULD NOT send an ICMP Redirect message; Redirects are to be sent only by gateways.' This confirms that End Systems are prohibited from sending ICMP redirect messages.
rules.test_hint: Configure an End System to attempt sending ICMP redirect messages and verify they are not transmitted
rules.source_quote: No ICMP redirect from ES

rules.name: ICMP Timestamp Request Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification explicitly states 'Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed' in the comments column for multiple ICMP-related TCP requirements. This clearly prohibits ICMP timestamp requests and other ICMP message types beyond echo request/reply.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP timestamp request messages and verify they are rejected or not processed
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.

rules.name: ICMP Timestamp Reply Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule correctly identifies that ICMP timestamp reply messages are prohibited. The specification clearly states in section 4.2.3.9 that 'Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.' This explicitly excludes all other ICMP message types, including timestamp replies. The extracted rule accurately captures this restriction as a boolean constraint (false = not allowed).
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP timestamp reply messages and verify they are rejected or not processed
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.

rules.name: ICMP Address Mask Request Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The text explicitly states 'Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.' in multiple places in the COMMENTS column for ICMP-related TCP requirements. This clearly prohibits ICMP address mask requests, as only echo request and echo reply messages are permitted.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP address mask request messages and verify they are rejected or not processed
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.

rules.name: ICMP Address Mask Reply Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification clearly states 'Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed' in the comments column for multiple TCP/ICMP interaction requirements. This definitively prohibits ICMP Address Mask Reply messages, which are not echo request or echo reply messages.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP address mask reply messages and verify they are rejected or not processed
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.

rules.name: Unauthorized Address Mask Reply Prohibition
rules.consensus_value: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks' appears in section 3.2.2.9 of the specification.
rules.test_hint: Configure a non-authoritative system to send address mask replies and verify this is prevented or rejected
rules.source_quote: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks.

rules.name: AFDX_LRU_interoperability
rules.consensus_value: Any AFDX-compliant LRU (including switch) must be connectable to any AFDX network if Form and Fit requirements are respected
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a genuine requirement from the specification. The source quote exactly matches the text in section 1.2 Scope (COMMENTARY), and the extracted behavioral constraint correctly represents the interoperability requirement that any AFDX-compliant LRU can be connected to any AFDX network provided Form and Fit requirements are met.
rules.source_quote: This means that any AFDX compliant LRU (including switch) can be connected to any AFDX network, as far as the Form and Fit requirements (specific to the System and not specified in this document) are respected.

rules.name: Integrity checking disablement per VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the text found in section 3.2.6.2.1 Integrity Checking, which clearly states that integrity checking can be disabled on a per VL basis through configuration.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with invalid sequence numbers for a VL with integrity checking disabled to test if they are accepted.
rules.source_quote: It should be possible on a per VL basis to disable the integrity checking on both networks through the configuration table.

rules.name: Interface ID Definition
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Support Local IP Multicasting
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD support
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'A host SHOULD support local IP multicasting on all connected networks for which a mapping from Class D IP addresses to link-layer addresses has been specified.' appears in the MULTICAST section of the requirements summary table.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send and receive multicast datagrams on a network and verify support.
rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD support local IP multicasting on all connected networks for which a mapping from Class D IP addresses to link-layer addresses has been specified.

rules.name: Join All-Hosts Group
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD join at startup
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'If IGMP is not implemented, a host SHOULD still join the "all-hosts" group (224.0.0.1) when the IP layer is initialized and remain a member for as long as the IP layer is active.' The extracted rule correctly captures this requirement as a SHOULD-level obligation for hosts to join the all-hosts group at startup when IGMP is not implemented.
rules.test_hint: Check if the host joins the all-hosts group at IP layer initialization without IGMP.
rules.source_quote: If IGMP is not implemented, a host SHOULD still join the 'all-hosts' group (224.0.0.1) when the IP layer is initialized and remain a member for as long as the IP layer is active.

rules.name: Pass IP Options to Transport Layer
rules.consensus_value: MUST pass all IP options to the transport layer
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The requirement that IP options must be passed to the transport layer is explicitly mentioned in the INTERFACES section.
rules.test_hint: Verify that all IP options in a received datagram are passed to the transport layer.
rules.source_quote: The parameter opt contains all the IP options received in the datagram; these MUST also be passed to the transport layer.

rules.name: Pass ICMP Messages to Transport Layer
rules.consensus_value: MUST pass certain ICMP messages to transport layer
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement clearly states that 'The IP layer MUST pass certain ICMP messages up to the appropriate transport-layer routine.' This is a behavioral requirement for the IP layer interface functionality.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages and check if they are passed to the transport layer.
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST pass certain ICMP messages up to the appropriate transport-layer routine.

rules.name: sequence number wraparound calculation
rules.consensus_value: wraparound from 254: PSN+1=255, PSN+2=1 (wraps at 256)
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: invalid frame discard rule
rules.consensus_value: frames not meeting sequence number criteria must be discarded
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes the integrity checking criteria (sequence number must be in interval [PSN+1, PSN+2] with special cases for RSN=0 and first frame after reset) and then explicitly states that frames not meeting these criteria are discarded.
