rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid sequence numbers and verify they are discarded by the receiving end system
rules.source_quote: Frames that do not meet these criteria are discarded.

rules.name: sequence number zero transmission after reset
rules.consensus_value: sequence number 0 is transmitted only after reset of transmitting equipment
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in Figure 3-17 which shows 'Reset of the Transmitting End System' where the sequence number goes from 255 to 0 after reset, with a note indicating ': reset of the transmitting equipment'. This demonstrates that sequence number 0 is transmitted only after a reset of the transmitting equipment.
rules.test_hint: Send sequence number 0 frames without preceding reset condition and verify proper handling
rules.source_quote: The sequence number 0 is transmitted only after a reset of the transmitting equipment.

rules.name: Discard Datagram With Bad Destination Address
rules.consensus_value: silently_discard_if_not_destined_for_host
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows 'Silently discard datagram with bad destination address 3.2.1.3' with an 'X' in the MUST column, and the accompanying text states 'A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram that is not destined for the host.' This matches exactly what the extracted rule describes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to IP addresses that are not assigned to any interface on the receiving end system
rules.source_quote: A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram that is not destined for the host.

rules.name: Support subnet addressing
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table shows 'Subnet addressing (RFC-950) 3.2.1.3' with an 'X' in the 'MUST' column, and the comment clearly states 'A host MUST support the subnet extensions to IP [IP:3].' This directly confirms that subnet addressing support is required with a boolean constraint value of true.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with subnet-specific addressing and verify the End System processes it correctly. Violation: send traffic with malformed subnet addressing.
rules.source_quote: A host MUST support the subnet extensions to IP [IP:3].

rules.name: Support IP reassembly
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table shows 'Support reassembly 3.2.1.4' with an 'X' in the 'MUST' column, and the comment states 'The Internet model requires that every host support Reassembly.' This clearly indicates that IP reassembly support is mandatory.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate fragmented IP datagrams and verify the receiving End System reassembles them correctly. Violation: send malformed fragments.
rules.source_quote: The Internet model requires that every host support Reassembly.

rules.name: Retain same Identification field for identical datagrams
rules.consensus_value: MAY optionally retain the same Identification field for identical datagrams
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table shows 'Retain same ID field in identical datagrams 3.2.1.5' with an 'X' in the 'NOT APPLICABLE' column, and includes the exact quote 'When sending an identical copy of an earlier datagram, a host MAY optionally retain the same Identification field in the copy.' This confirms that AFDX systems may optionally retain the same Identification field for identical datagrams, making this a valid behavioral constraint.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate identical datagrams with different Identification fields and observe if the End System handles them correctly. Violation: enforce strict retention when not required.
rules.source_quote: When sending an identical copy of an earlier datagram, a host MAY optionally retain the same Identification field in the copy.

rules.name: Do not implement RFC-795 TOS mappings
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD NOT implement RFC-795 link-layer mappings for TOS
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that RFC-795 link-layer mappings for TOS SHOULD NOT be implemented, which matches exactly with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can verify that the End System does not apply RFC-795 TOS mappings. Violation: apply RFC-795 mappings incorrectly.
rules.source_quote: The particular link-layer mappings of TOS contained in RFC-795 SHOULD NOT be implemented.

rules.name: Stream Identifier option handling
rules.consensus_value: MUST silently ignore Stream Identifier option if received; SHOULD NOT send it
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. Section 3.2.1.8a states 'This option is obsolete; it SHOULD NOT be sent…' and section 3.2.1.8b states '...and it MUST be silently ignored if received'. The extracted rule correctly captures both the SHOULD NOT send and MUST silently ignore requirements for the Stream Identifier option.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a datagram with the Stream Identifier option and verify it is silently ignored.
rules.source_quote: This option is obsolete; it SHOULD NOT be sent… and it MUST be silently ignored if received.

rules.name: Non-redundant return route construction
rules.consensus_value: MUST build correct (non-redundant) return route even if recorded route includes source host
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the requirement found in section 3.2.1.8c regarding building correct return source routes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a Source Route option with redundant entries and verify the return route is correctly formed.
rules.source_quote: When a Return source route is built, it MUST be correctly formed even if the recorded route included the source host.

rules.name: Manual Configuration Method Requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The table clearly shows 'A manual method of entering this configuration data MUST be provided.' in section 3.3.1.6, and it's marked as 'NOT APPLICABLE' for AFDX because 'AFDX is statically defined, no default gateways'.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send traffic without manual configuration or with invalid manual configuration to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: A manual method of entering this configuration data MUST be provided.

rules.name: Ignore unknown TCP options
rules.consensus_value: TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement is found in section 4.2.3.8 under 'IP OPTIONS' where it clearly states 'TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.' However, there is a minor categorization issue - this rule should be categorized as 'TCP Options Handling' rather than 'IP Options Handling' since it deals with TCP's handling of IP options passed up from the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with unknown options and check if they are ignored.
rules.source_quote: TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.

rules.name: Source-routed datagram forwarding
rules.consensus_value: A host may act as an intermediate hop in a source route, forwarding a source-routed datagram to the next specified hop.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text on page 129. The source quote exactly matches the text in the specification: 'Subject to restrictions given below, a host MAY be able to act as an intermediate hop in a source route, forwarding a source-routed datagram to the next specified hop.' The behavioral constraint accurately captures this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Generate a source-routed datagram and verify if the host forwards it as an intermediate hop.
rules.source_quote: Subject to restrictions given below, a host MAY be able to act as an intermediate hop in a source route, forwarding a source-routed datagram to the next specified hop.

rules.name: Update Timestamp option
rules.consensus_value: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Timestamp Option must add the current timestamp to that option.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that a host forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Timestamp Option MUST add the current timestamp to that option, according to the rules for this option. The extracted rule accurately captures this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a Timestamp option and verify if the current timestamp is added upon forwarding.
rules.source_quote: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Timestamp Option MUST add the current timestamp to that option, according to the rules for this option.

rules.name: Address mask usage in local/remote decision
rules.consensus_value: MUST use address mask in local/remote decision for outbound datagrams
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Use address mask in local/remote decision 3.3.1.1' as a requirement, and the subsequent text explains 'To decide if the destination is on a connected network, the following algorithm MUST be used.' This confirms that address masks must be used in routing decisions to determine if destinations are local or remote.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate outbound IP datagrams with destination addresses and observe if the AFDX End System correctly uses the address mask to determine if the destination is local or remote.
rules.source_quote: Use address mask in local/remote decision

rules.name: IP Source Address Class A Private Format
rules.consensus_value: Class A private address with first 8 bits '00001010'
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 3.4.1.4.1 explicitly states 'The IP address should be Class A and private Internet Unicast Address (First 8 bits should be '0000 1010').' The extracted rule correctly identifies this as a format constraint for IP source addresses requiring the first 8 bits to be '00001010' (Class A private address format).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with IP source addresses that don't match the Class A private format (e.g., Class B, Class C, or non-private addresses)
rules.source_quote: The IP address should be Class A and private Internet Unicast Address (First 8 bits should be '0000 1010').

rules.name: IP Address Spare Field Default Value
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The Spare field is normally not used and set to zero as shown in Figure 3-37.' Additionally, Figure 3-37 shows the Spare Field Meaning as '0 0 0 No significance', confirming that the spare field should be set to zero (value 0).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in the 3-bit spare field of the IP address
rules.source_quote: The Spare field is normally not used and set to zero as shown in Figure 3-37.

rules.name: IP Multicast Address Class D Format
rules.consensus_value: Class D with first 4 bits '1110'
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. Figure 3-38 clearly shows the IP Multicast Addressing Format with the first 4 bits labeled as 'Class D "1110"'. This explicitly states that IP multicast addresses must use the Class D format with the first 4 bits set to '1110'.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with multicast addresses that don't have the proper Class D format (first 4 bits not '1110')
rules.source_quote: Class D "1110" IP Multicast Identifier

rules.name: Default Time to Live
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows that TTL (Time to Live) is 'Not used in AFDX, default value is 1' in the comments column for the 'Configurable Time to Live' requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with TTL value other than 1
rules.source_quote: Not used in AFDX, default value is 1

rules.name: IP Version Field Validation
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows the requirement 'Silently discard if IP version is not equal to 4' with reference to section 3.2.1.1, and includes the exact quote 'A datagram whose version number is not 4 MUST be silently discarded.' The rule correctly identifies that only IP version 4 is allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with version field set to values other than 4 (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 15)
rules.source_quote: A datagram whose version number is not 4 MUST be silently discarded.

rules.name: IP Header Checksum Verification
rules.consensus_value: must_verify_and_discard_on_error
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows that verifying IP checksum and silently discarding bad datagrams is a MUST requirement from RFC-1122 section 3.2.1.2, and the comment column provides the exact quote that matches the rule's source_quote.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with intentionally corrupted header checksums
rules.source_quote: A host MUST verify the IP header checksum on every received datagram and silently discard every datagram that has a bad checksum.

rules.name: TTL Minimum Acceptance Rule
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The text clearly states 'A host MUST NOT discard a datagram just because it was received with TTL less than 2.' This means datagrams with TTL=1 must be accepted, which aligns with the extracted rule's constraint of TTL ≥1.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with TTL=1 to verify they are not discarded based solely on low TTL value
rules.source_quote: A host MUST NOT discard a datagram just because it was received with TTL less than 2.

rules.name: IPv4 Packet Structure Compliance
rules.consensus_value: Packets must comply with Figure 3-30
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'IPv4 packet structure should be compliant with Figure 3-30' in section 3.3.3.2 ES IP Profile. The rule correctly captures this behavioral requirement for IPv4 packet structure compliance.
rules.test_hint: Generate packets that do not comply with the specified structure to test compliance.
rules.source_quote: IPv4 packet structure should be compliant with Figure 3-30.

rules.name: IPv4 Total Length Field Range
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number' in section 3.3.3.2 ES IP Profile.
rules.test_hint: Send packets with Total Length outside the range [21, 1499] to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number.

rules.name: Valid IP source address requirement for transmission
rules.consensus_value: must_be_host_address
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement that when a host sends a UDP datagram, the source address MUST be one of the IP addresses of the host is clearly documented in section 4.1.3.6 of the UDP requirements.
rules.test_hint: Verify that outgoing UDP datagrams use only valid host IP addresses as source addresses, not foreign or invalid addresses
rules.source_quote: When a host sends a UDP datagram, the source address MUST be (one of) the IP address(es) of the host.

rules.name: Unknown IP Options Handling
rules.consensus_value: silently_ignore_unknown_options
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 3.2.1.8 explicitly states 'The IP and transport layer MUST each interpret those IP options that they understand and silently ignore the others.' This confirms that unknown IP options must be silently ignored.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with unrecognized option types to verify they are silently ignored without generating errors
rules.source_quote: The IP and transport layer MUST each interpret those IP options that they understand and silently ignore the others.

rules.name: Stream Identifier Option Handling
rules.consensus_value: silently_ignore_if_received
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The table clearly shows 'Silently ignore Stream Identifier option 3.2.1.8b X' with the requirement '...and it MUST be silently ignored if received.' This directly matches the extracted rule's behavioral constraint of 'silently_ignore_if_received'.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams containing Stream Identifier option to verify it is silently ignored
rules.source_quote: ...and it MUST be silently ignored if received.

rules.name: Multiple Source Route Options Prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'An IP header containing more than one Source Route option MUST NOT be sent.' This directly supports the extracted rule that prohibits multiple source route options (≤1 constraint).
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with multiple Source Route options to test rejection or handling
rules.source_quote: An IP header containing more than one Source Route option MUST NOT be sent.

rules.name: Constant end-to-end latency in point-to-point system
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that in the point-to-point system described, 'the time taken to deliver a message, through the network, from the emitter to the receiver is constant.' This establishes that constant end-to-end latency is indeed a characteristic of the point-to-point ARINC 429 bus system being compared to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce variable delays in frame transmission or switching to violate the constant latency rule and observe if the network detects or compensates for the violation.
rules.source_quote: the time taken to deliver a message, through the network, from the emitter to the receiver is constant

rules.name: Jitter Time Calculation
rules.consensus_value: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The formula Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap is explicitly provided for calculating jitter time when simultaneous reception of frames occurs at a switch.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with varying sizes (M) and observe the jitter time (Tj) to ensure it follows the formula.
rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c, with a maximum jitter dependent on the message length: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap

rules.name: Latency for First Frame
rules.consensus_value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 x M)/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The formula for latency of the first frame is clearly provided with the exact same mathematical expression and variable definitions.
rules.test_hint: Send a single frame and measure the latency to ensure it matches the calculated La.
rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.name: Latency for Delayed Frame
rules.consensus_value: Lb = La + Tj
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The formula Lb = La + Tj is directly quoted from the document under 'Latency for the delayed frame' section.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames and measure the latency of the delayed frame to ensure it matches the calculated Lb.
rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame: Lb = La + Tj

rules.name: MAC Source Address Format
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the MAC source address format as specified in section 3.2.5.2. The format string correctly represents the structure shown in Figure 3-11, including the constant field '0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000', the User_Defined_ID field (nnnn nnnn nnnn nnnn), the Interface_ID field (mmm), and the final constant field (0 0000). The source quote correctly identifies the constant field value and the meaning of the least significant bits.
rules.test_hint: Use a MAC source address that does not comply with the specified format to test system handling.
rules.source_quote: The Constant field is set to “0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000” as shown in Figure 3-11. The least significant bit of the first byte indicates the Individual Address = 0. The second to least significant bit of the first byte indicates the locally administered address = 1.

rules.name: Transmission Continuity on Link Failure
rules.consensus_value: true
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.' This is a mandatory behavior requirement for ES MAC profile, making it a genuine protocol rule.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a link failure and check if transmission continues.
rules.source_quote: All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.

rules.name: Minimum frame overhead calculation
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in section 3.2.4.2 of the specification. The calculation '64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes' is quoted verbatim from the specification text and represents the minimum frame overhead calculation for determining maximum frame rate at 100 Mbps.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with incorrect overhead calculations or violate the IFG, preamble, or SFD requirements
rules.source_quote: 64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes to transmit at 100 Mbits/s.

rules.name: Minimum frame transmission duration
rules.justification: The rule correctly extracts the minimum frame transmission duration of 6.72 μs from the specification. The specification explicitly states this value when calculating the maximum frame rate for the shortest frame (64 bytes) plus overhead (IFG, Preamble, SFD) totaling 84 bytes at 100 Mbits/s, which equals 6.72 μs per frame.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with transmission durations shorter than 6.72 μs to violate timing constraints
rules.source_quote: Equivalent to a duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).

rules.name: message_padding_for_bandwidth_allocation
rules.consensus_value: Unused portions of a message should be padded to maintain fixed bandwidth allocation.
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification clearly states that unused portions of messages should be filled with binary zeros (padding) to maintain the fixed bandwidth allocation. The behavioral constraint accurately captures this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can omit padding or use non-zero padding values in messages.
rules.source_quote: The bandwidth has been allocated to this data flow for the maximum size the message can be, and is not useable by any other flow. It is therefore not wasted.

rules.name: variable_length_opaque_structure_constraint
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The text clearly states 'Variable Length Opaque-Static Length = 40 bytes' in the figure description, establishing a maximum constraint of 40 bytes for variable length opaque structures.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate opaque structures exceeding 40 bytes or with malformed length fields.
rules.source_quote: Variable Length Opaque-Static Length = 40 bytes

rules.name: dynamic_message_length_constraint
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately extracted. The specification explicitly states 'Dynamic Length = 22' in the context of an ARINC 429 to AFDX message formatting example. This establishes a clear constraint that dynamic length equals 22 bytes for this specific message format.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate dynamic-length messages exceeding 22 bytes.
rules.source_quote: Dynamic Length = 22

rules.name: Reserved Field Content
rules.consensus_value: binary zeros
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text explicitly states that '32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros' in section 1-3.5. The rule correctly identifies this as a format constraint requiring binary zeros content.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with the reserved field filled with non-zero values and observe if the network processes them correctly.
rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: Global Spare Field Content
rules.consensus_value: binary zeros
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly mentions a 'Global Spare field' as an optional field that can be included in messages, and specifically states that 'If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.' The rule accurately captures both the field name and the requirement for binary zeros content.
rules.test_hint: Include a global spare field in frames and fill it with non-zero values to test if the network processes them correctly.
rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: Reserved word alignment requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement for 32-bit alignment of the Reserved word is clearly mentioned in the Data Alignment section.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where the Reserved word is not aligned on a 32-bit boundary
rules.source_quote: The Reserved word at the beginning of the message should be aligned on a 32-bit boundary.

rules.name: Functional Status Sets alignment requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.' This is a direct requirement for data alignment of Functional Status Sets to 32-bit boundaries.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where Functional Status Sets are not aligned on 32-bit boundaries
rules.source_quote: Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.

rules.name: Data element alignment by size
rules.consensus_value: address_divisible_by_element_length
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The quote exactly matches the text in section 1-3.2 Data Alignment, which defines what it means for a data element to be aligned in memory. The behavioral constraint 'address_divisible_by_element_length' accurately captures the requirement that the address must be evenly divisible by the data element length in bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send messages with data elements not aligned according to their size (e.g., 4-byte value not on address divisible by 4)
rules.source_quote: A data element is said to be aligned if the address of the element in memory is evenly divisible by the data element length (in bytes).

rules.name: ARINC 429 data conversion preference
rules.consensus_value: ARINC 429 data should be converted to permitted AFDX data elements at gateway
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's recommendation for handling ARINC 429 data in AFDX networks. The extracted behavioral constraint correctly reflects that ARINC 429 data should be converted to permitted AFDX data elements at the gateway, and the emphasis on making 'every effort' to do this conversion is properly captured.
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 data that is not converted to permitted AFDX data elements and verify gateway behavior
rules.source_quote: The preferred way to put ARINC 429 data on an AFDX network is to convert the individual parameters into one of the permitted AFDX data elements of Table 1-1.0. Every effort should be made to do this at the gateway where ARINC 429 and AFDX meet.

rules.name: Single label message structure
rules.consensus_value: 32-bit opaque data primitive for single ARINC 429 label
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes 'Approach 1: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive' and specifically mentions this structure should be used for single label messages. The 32-bit format is confirmed by the message structure diagram showing the A429 Label at specific byte offsets (0x00000004 to 0x00000008, which is 4 bytes = 32 bits).
rules.test_hint: Send single ARINC 429 labels in formats other than 32-bit opaque data primitive
rules.source_quote: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive

rules.name: Variable length multiple label structure
rules.consensus_value: variable length opaque structure for multiple ARINC 429 labels
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. Approach 2 specifically describes placing 'a varying number of labels in a variable length opaque structure' as one of two general approaches for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple ARINC 429 labels in fixed length structures instead of variable length
rules.source_quote: Place a varying number of labels in a variable length opaque structure

rules.name: Reply with Same Address as Specified Destination Address
rules.consensus_value: Source address for response should be the specific-destination address of the request
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows under the MULTIHOMING section that 'If the datagram is sent in response to a received datagram, the source address for the response SHOULD be the specific-destination address of the request.' The rule correctly captures this behavioral requirement, including the proper use of SHOULD rather than MUST.
rules.test_hint: Send requests and verify if responses use the specified destination address as the source.
rules.source_quote: If the datagram is sent in response to a received datagram, the source address for the response SHOULD be the specific-destination address of the request.

rules.name: FIFO Message Ordering
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly mandates that queuing service must use FIFO (First In, First Out) discipline for message ordering in both transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple messages through queuing service and verify they are received in the same order (FIFO)
rules.source_quote: To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.

rules.name: Functional Status Set field size
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly and clearly stated in the specification. The text directly states 'The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields' which confirms both the field size (32 bits) and validates the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with FSS fields that are not exactly 32 bits in size
rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields

rules.name: Status field size within FSS
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines that 'The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields', which confirms that each status field within the FSS is exactly 8 bits in size.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with status fields within FSS that are not 8 bits each
rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields

rules.name: Unused status fields must be zero
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly mandates that when only one Data Set is used in a Functional Data Set, the remaining 24 bits (3 status fields of 8 bits each) of the 32-bit Functional Status Set must be zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames where unused status fields in FSS contain non-zero values
rules.source_quote: If no other DS are used in a FDS, the remaining 24 bits of the FSS must be zeros

rules.name: Maximum data sets per FSS
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text explicitly states that the Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8-bit status fields, where 'The first status field is used to represent the health and status of the first DS. If no other DS are used in a FDS, the remaining 24 bits' are available. This clearly indicates that each status field corresponds to one data set, and with 4 status fields total, the maximum number of data sets per FSS is 4.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with more than 4 data sets associated with a single FSS
rules.source_quote: each of the remaining status fields are used to represent health and status for them, up to 4 DS

rules.name: restrict outgoing datagrams to correct interface
rules.consensus_value: send_only_through_matching_interface
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote appears in the multihoming section where it states '(B) A host MAY restrict itself to sending (non-source-routed) IP datagrams only through the physical interface that corresponds to the IP source address of the datagrams.' The rule correctly captures this behavioral constraint that allows a host to validate that outgoing datagrams are sent through the interface that matches their source address.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send IP datagrams with source addresses that don't match the outgoing interface to test source address validation
rules.source_quote: A host MAY restrict itself to sending (non-source-routed) IP datagrams only through the physical interface that corresponds to the IP source address of the datagrams

rules.name: Label ordering in gateway transmission
rules.consensus_value: Labels presented in order received by gateway for transparent operation
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a behavioral requirement explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that labels are presented in the order received by the gateway to maintain transparency of the gateway and AFDX network operation.
rules.test_hint: Send labels in different order than received at gateway and verify consumer processing
rules.source_quote: The labels are presented in the order received by the gateway so the gateway and AFDX network are essentially transparent.

rules.name: Label placement in opaque structure
rules.consensus_value: Labels placed one after another beginning with byte after length and pad fields
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly describes how labels are placed in the opaque structure for the variable length approach (Approach 2).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with labels placed in incorrect positions within the opaque structure
rules.source_quote: As labels arrive at the gateway, they are placed one after another in the opaque structure beginning with the byte after the length field and pad field.

rules.name: Length field computation
rules.consensus_value: Gateway computes bytes of static length with good data and loads into length field
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavior described in the specification. The text explicitly states that 'When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure.' This is a specific behavioral rule for how gateways should compute and set the length field value in variable length ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect length field values that don't match actual data content
rules.source_quote: When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure.

rules.name: Unused portion padding
rules.consensus_value: unused portion of opaque field filled with binary zeros
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that when using variable length opaque structures for ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting, the unused portion of the opaque field must be filled with binary zeros. This is a specific formatting requirement for ensuring consistent message structure.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in unused portions of opaque fields
rules.source_quote: The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros.

rules.name: Complete structure transmission
rules.consensus_value: Entire static structure transmitted, not just used portion
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that when transmitting variable length structures, the entire static structure must be sent, not just the portion containing valid data.
rules.test_hint: Send frames containing only the used portion of structure instead of entire static structure
rules.source_quote: The message is then sent, with the entire static structure, not just the used portion.

rules.name: Bounded End-to-End Latency
rules.consensus_value: A firm, mathematically provable upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay must be guaranteed.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a core requirement from the AFDX specification. The specification explicitly states that 'A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay' and that 'a maximum network transit delay (also called end-to-end latency) must be guaranteed.' This is a fundamental behavioral constraint that defines the deterministic nature of AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic patterns that cause latency to exceed the guaranteed upper bound (e.g., by overloading switches or violating BAG).
rules.source_quote: A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay.

rules.name: Bounded Delay Jitter for Flow
rules.consensus_value: A bound to the delay jitter for a flow must be mathematically computable, though not fixed.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a key statement from the specification about delay jitter bounds. The specification explicitly states that while particular delay jitter is not fixed and depends on global network traffic, a bound to the delay jitter can be mathematically computed. This is a genuine behavioral requirement for AFDX flows.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic that causes delay jitter to exceed the computed bound (e.g., by introducing variable delays or congestion).
rules.source_quote: Particular delay jitter for a flow (end-to-end transit delay variation between any two frames of the same flow) is not fixed since it depends on the global network traffic at a given time. Nevertheless, a bound to the delay jitter can be mathematically computed.

rules.name: IP version compliance
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Section 3.3.3.2 ES IP Profile clearly states 'The packet structure version should be IPv4.' This directly supports the rule that the IP version field must be IPv4.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate IPv6 packets or malformed IPv4 headers.
rules.source_quote: The packet structure version should be IPv4.

rules.name: IPv4 total length range
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that in AFDX, the IPv4 Total Length field range is from 21 to 1499 bytes, which is different from the ordinary IPv4 range of 21 to 1500 bytes due to the Sequence Number in the Redundancy Management Function.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate IPv4 packets with Total Length outside the 21-1499 byte range.
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number (see Section 3.2.6.2.2, Redundancy Management Function).

rules.name: Log discarded datagrams
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD provide capability to log discarded datagrams, including contents
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text clearly shows in the requirements table under section 3.1: 'However, for diagnosis of problems a host SHOULD provide the capability of logging the error (see Section 1.2.3), including the contents of the silently-discarded datagram...' This matches exactly with the extracted rule's constraint value.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate invalid datagrams and verify they are logged when discarded. Violation: discard datagrams without logging.
rules.source_quote: However, for diagnosis of problems a host SHOULD provide the capability of logging the error (see Section 1.2.3), including the contents of the silently-discarded datagram…

rules.name: Record discarded datagrams in counter
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD record discarded datagrams in a statistics counter
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The table shows an entry for 'Record in counter 3.1' with an 'X' in the MUST column and the comment 'loged in MIB'. The corresponding requirement text states '...and SHOULD record the event in a statistics counter.' This confirms that discarded datagrams should be recorded in a statistics counter.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate invalid datagrams and verify the discard count increments. Violation: discard datagrams without updating the counter.
rules.source_quote: …and SHOULD record the event in a statistics counter.

rules.name: Monitoring Function Required
rules.consensus_value: AFDX switches must implement monitoring functionality
rules.justification: The rule is genuine. Section 4.6 'Monitoring Function' is explicitly listed in the table of contents, indicating that AFDX switches must implement monitoring functionality as a required function alongside other mandatory functions like filtering, policing, and switching.
rules.test_hint: Verify that switches provide monitoring capabilities for network health and performance tracking
rules.source_quote: 4.6 Monitoring Function

rules.name: TCP transport protocol optionality
rules.justification: The rule correctly identifies that TCP transport protocol is optional in AFDX. The specification explicitly states 'Transport: UDP, TCP (optional)' in section 1.2, which directly supports this rule. The boolean constraint value of 'false' appropriately represents that TCP is not mandatory (i.e., it's optional).
rules.test_hint: Send TCP frames to devices that may not implement TCP support and verify proper handling
rules.source_quote: Transport: UDP, TCP (optional)

rules.name: AFDX LRU network interoperability requirement
rules.consensus_value: any AFDX compliant LRU can connect to any AFDX network
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in section 1.2 of the specification. The text clearly establishes that AFDX compliance ensures interoperability across any AFDX network, subject only to Form and Fit requirements which are system-specific and outside the scope of this document.
rules.test_hint: Test cross-vendor LRU compatibility by connecting devices from different manufacturers and verifying proper network operation
rules.source_quote: This means that any AFDX compliant LRU (including switch) can be connected to any AFDX network, as far as the Form and Fit requirements (specific to the System and not specified in this document) are respected.

rules.name: Physical layer specification requirement
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately extracted. The specification explicitly states in section 1.2 that 'Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.' This establishes a clear requirement that the physical layer must conform to ARINC 664 Part 2 solutions, even though Part 7 itself doesn't specify the physical layer details.
rules.test_hint: Test network behavior with physical layer implementations that do not conform to ARINC 664 Part 2
rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.name: Technological latency upper bound in transmission
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the technological latency requirement for transmission as stated in section 3.2.4.1. The specification clearly states that 'The technological latency of the end-system in transmission should be bounded and lower than 150 μs + frame delay.' The extracted rule correctly identifies this as an upper bound constraint with the formula '150 + frame_delay' in microseconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate an end system introducing latency exceeding 150 μs + frame_delay for a transmitted frame.
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in transmission should be bounded and lower than 150 μs + frame delay.

rules.name: Maximum allowed jitter in transmission (formula 1)
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in section 3.2.4.3 of the specification. The formula 'max_jitter ≤ 40 + (8 * Lmax) / (Nbw / 1000000)' matches exactly what is shown in the specification text, and the variable units are correctly identified (max_jitter in μs, Lmax in octets, Nbw in bits/s).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with jitter exceeding the value calculated by the formula for a given Lmax and Nbw.
rules.source_quote: In transmission, the maximum allowed jitter on each VL at the output of the end-system should comply with both of the following formulas: ... max_jitter ≤ 40 + (8 * Lmax) / (Nbw / 1000000).

rules.name: Global jitter upper bound
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'In all cases, the jitter is bounded at 500μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network.' This establishes a global maximum jitter bound of 500 microseconds that applies universally across the network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with jitter exceeding 500 μs on a single VL.
rules.source_quote: In all cases, the jitter is bounded at 500μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network.

rules.name: Physical Layer Compatibility
rules.consensus_value: Must be compatible with ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly says 'Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.' This establishes a behavioral requirement for physical layer compatibility with ARINC 664 Part 2 solutions.
rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.name: INIT Operating Mode Required
rules.consensus_value: AFDX devices must support INIT operating mode
rules.justification: The specification clearly includes INIT as one of the operating modes in section 4.8.2. The table of contents shows '4.8.2 INIT' with subsections for initialization sequence and ground condition, confirming that AFDX devices must support this operating mode. The rule correctly identifies this as a required behavioral constraint.
rules.test_hint: Test device behavior during initialization - verify proper startup sequence and that device enters operational state correctly
rules.source_quote: 4.8.2  INIT

rules.name: OPS Operating Mode Required
rules.consensus_value: AFDX devices must support OPS (Operational) mode
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. Section 4.8.3 explicitly defines OPS (Operational Mode) and describes that switches should enter this mode after initialization when conditions are met. The specification clearly indicates that OPS mode is a required operational state where the switch performs its normal functions.
rules.test_hint: Test normal operational behavior - verify device processes frames correctly when in operational mode
rules.source_quote: 4.8.3  OPS: Operational Mode

rules.name: Frame Order Preservation Within Virtual Link
rules.consensus_value: maintain_ordinal_integrity_within_VL
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'For this reason AFDX requires ordinal integrity of frames within a Virtual Link.' This is a behavioral requirement that frames transmitted on a Virtual Link must arrive in the same order they were sent.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL and verify they arrive in the same order, or deliberately reorder frames to test violation detection
rules.source_quote: For this reason AFDX requires ordinal integrity of frames within a Virtual Link.

rules.name: Default physical port number
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 4.7.2.1 of the specification. The text clearly indicates that 'Port # 1 is the default external physical port used to communicate with the End System of the Switch.' This establishes port number 1 as the default physical port, making the constraint of allowed values [1] accurate.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when frames arrive on ports other than port 1 during default configuration state
rules.source_quote: Port # 1 is the default external physical port used to communicate with the End System of the Switch.

rules.name: Auto negotiation disabled on default port
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 4.7.2.1 of the specification. The text clearly states that 'The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.' This directly confirms that auto negotiation should be disabled (false) on the default port.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when auto negotiation is enabled on the default port
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: Switch enters INIT mode after power rise or reset
rules.consensus_value: switch must enter INIT mode after power rise or reset
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly and clearly stated in the specification. The exact phrase 'The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset' appears in section 4.8.1 Overview, and this behavior is further confirmed in section 4.8.2 which states 'INIT is the default mode in which the Switch enters after power rise or after a reset.'
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior immediately after simulated power cycle or reset to verify it enters INIT mode
rules.source_quote: The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset.

rules.name: PASSIVE mode stops all functions except network management
rules.consensus_value: only network management communication allowed, all other functions stopped
rules.justification: The rule accurately reflects the specification's description of PASSIVE MODE behavior. The spec explicitly states that in PASSIVE MODE, the Switch only offers the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function and all other functions should be stopped.
rules.test_hint: When switch is in PASSIVE mode, verify that normal frame forwarding is stopped while network management remains accessible
rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE MODE, the Switch only offers the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function), all others functions should be stopped.

rules.name: QUIET mode entry on catastrophic failure
rules.consensus_value: enter QUIET mode on catastrophic failure that makes functional behavior questionable
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly defines when QUIET mode is entered and the behavioral requirement is accurately captured.
rules.test_hint: Simulate catastrophic failures or corrupted configurations to verify switch enters QUIET mode and stops normal operation
rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable

rules.name: physical_layer_compliance
rules.consensus_value: ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately extracted. The specification explicitly states in section 1.2 Scope (COMMENTARY) that 'Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.' This establishes a clear constraint that the physical layer must comply with ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.
rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.name: No Shared Transmit Ports
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'Having two data sources for one transmit AFDX com or SAP port may also result in a loss of data' and 'The examples with red cross should not be used.' This establishes that shared transmit ports are prohibited, making the boolean constraint value of 'false' for shared_transmit_port correct.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate two data sources transmitting to the same AFDX port, violating the no-sharing rule.
rules.source_quote: Having two data sources for one transmit AFDX com or SAP port may also result in a loss of data... The examples with red cross should not be used.

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Transmit_Configuration_Frozen
rules.consensus_value: frozen_by_configuration
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a behavioral constraint explicitly stated in the specification. Section 3.4.1.5 clearly states that 'The transmission and the reception path is frozen by configuration' when describing AFDX Communication Port characteristics.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the transmit configuration (e.g., UDP source port or destination IP) is dynamically altered during operation.
rules.source_quote: The transmission and the reception path is frozen by configuration.

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Transmit_Link_Constraint
rules.consensus_value: single_set_per_port
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 3.4.1.5.1 explicitly states 'In transmission, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination and UDP destination.' This establishes a behavioral constraint that each AFDX Communication Port in transmission mode must be associated with only one unique combination of these five parameters.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where an AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple sets of (UDP source port, IP source, VL, IP destination, UDP destination).
rules.source_quote: In transmission, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination and UDP destination.

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Receive_Link_Constraint
rules.consensus_value: single_set_per_port
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines that in reception, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set consisting of unique UDP port destination, IP destination, and VL (MAC destination).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where an AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple sets of (UDP destination port, IP destination, VL).
rules.source_quote: In reception, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set (unique UDP port destination, IP destination, VL (MAC destination)) and additionally to the Ethernet physical interface if the redundancy management is disabling.

rules.name: SAP_Port_Transmit_Quadruplet_Configuration
rules.consensus_value: frozen_by_configuration
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The quote matches exactly with the source text describing SAP port transmission behavior.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the transmit quadruplet (e.g., UDP source port or MAC destination) is dynamically altered during operation.
rules.source_quote: In transmission, the SAP port uses by configuration a frozen quadruplet (UDP Port source address, IP source address, Mac Source address, MAC destination address (VL identification)).

rules.name: Allowed Port Number Range
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The quote from the specification clearly states that 'Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.' This confirms both the field name (port_number), the data type (range), and the constraint values (1 to 65535).
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic using port numbers outside the range 1 to 65535 to test network behavior.
rules.source_quote: Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.

rules.name: Continuous transmission on link failure
rules.consensus_value: continue_transmitting_on_physical_failure
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly and clearly stated in the specification. The behavioral requirement that End Systems must continue transmitting even during physical layer link failures is directly quoted from section 3.3.3.1. The commentary explains this is to avoid sending old buffered frames after link recovery and to prevent failure propagation.
rules.test_hint: Simulate physical layer link failures and verify that End System continues attempting transmission instead of buffering frames
rules.source_quote: All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.

rules.name: Port operational state
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. In section 4.7.3.2, the document clearly lists 'Port State (ON/ OFF)' as one of the parameters required on a per port basis for the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to ports configured as OFF to verify they are not forwarded
rules.source_quote: Port State (ON/ OFF)

rules.name: port_speed_configuration
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The quote provided in the rule exactly matches the text in section 4.11.2, and the allowed values of 10 Mbps and 100 Mbps are correctly extracted from the specification.
rules.test_hint: Configure ports to unsupported speeds and verify rejection
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: full_duplex_requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly requires that 'Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.' This clearly mandates full duplex operation and prohibits auto negotiation, making the constraint that only 'full_duplex' is allowed accurate.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure half-duplex mode and verify rejection
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: auto_negotiation_prohibition
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Section 4.11.2 clearly states that 'Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.' This directly prohibits auto-negotiation functionality.
rules.test_hint: Enable auto-negotiation and verify it is not used or is rejected
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: Specification precedence over IEEE 802.3
rules.consensus_value: In case of conflict between ARINC 664 Part 7 and IEEE 802.3, ARINC 664 Part 7 takes precedence.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the document precedence policy stated in section 1.5. The specification explicitly states that in case of conflict between ARINC 664 Part 7 and applicable ISO and IEEE standards (which includes IEEE 802.3), ARINC 664 Part 7 takes precedence.
rules.source_quote: In case of a conflict between this Specification and the applicable ISO and IEEE standards, this Specification should have precedence.

rules.name: Restriction of IEEE 802.3 options
rules.consensus_value: ARINC 664 Part 7 restricts IEEE 802.3 options to remove ambiguity or address aeronautical environment conflicts.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's philosophy as stated in section 1.5. The constraint correctly describes that ARINC 664 Part 7 only restricts IEEE 802.3 options when necessary due to aeronautical environment conflicts or to remove ambiguity.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic using unsupported IEEE 802.3 options (e.g., non-standard frame sizes or protocols) to test if the network rejects or ignores them.
rules.source_quote: The philosophy of this Specification is to define changes to the provisions of IEEE 802.3 only when the aeronautical environment or user desires conflict with the provisions of IEEE 802.3, or when it is necessary to remove ambiguity by restricting the options available to implementers.

rules.name: UDP Port Usage for AFDX Communication Ports
rules.consensus_value: AFDX communication ports must be defined through UDP ports, which can be either transmitters or receivers.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote matches the rule description that AFDX communication ports are defined through UDP ports and can be either transmitters or receivers.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with invalid or undefined UDP ports for AFDX communication ports.
rules.source_quote: AFDX communication ports are defined through UDP ports. Such ports can be either transmitters or receivers.

rules.name: Queuing Mode for Bi-Directional Communication
rules.consensus_value: For bi-directional communication using conventional AFDX communication ports, the ports must be used in queuing mode.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The extracted behavioral constraint accurately reflects the requirement that for bi-directional communication using conventional AFDX communication ports, queuing mode must be used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames for bi-directional communication using ports not configured in queuing mode.
rules.source_quote: For a bi-directional communication, the ports should be used in queuing mode.

rules.name: TCP sender buffering prohibition
rules.consensus_value: MUST NOT buffer data indefinitely if PUSH flag cannot be implemented
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in Table 2-1. The specification clearly shows that for TCP PUSH flag handling, when a TCP implementation cannot implement PUSH flags on SEND calls, the sending TCP '(1) must not buffer data indefinitely'. This is marked with 'X' in the 'MUST NOT' column, confirming it's a prohibition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP traffic where data is buffered indefinitely, violating the prohibition.
rules.source_quote: If cannot, sender buffer indefinitely 4.2.2.2   X  ...then the sending TCP: (1) must not buffer data indefinitely…

rules.name: TCP PUSH flag notification to application layer
rules.consensus_value: OPTIONAL (not enforced as MUST or MUST NOT)
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The table clearly shows that 'Notify receiving application of PUSH' has an 'X' in the 'MUST' column, and the comments section explicitly states 'Passing a received PSH flag to the application layer is now OPTIONAL.' This indicates the behavior is optional rather than mandatory.
rules.source_quote: Notify receiving application of PUSH 4.2.2.2 X  Passing a received PSH flag to the application layer is now OPTIONAL.

rules.name: AFDX_protocol_restrictions_for_data_transport
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from Table D-1 in Appendix D. The table shows that for 'Data Transport (simple)' service, only UDP protocol is marked with 'X', indicating it is the only allowed protocol for simple data transport in AFDX networks. TCP is not marked for this service, confirming that UDP is the exclusive protocol for simple data transport.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames using TCP for simple data transport instead of UDP.
rules.source_quote: Data Transport (simple)    X                (UDP only in Table D-1).

rules.name: TCP must set PUSH bit in last buffered segment
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The TCP requirements table clearly states 'MUST set the PSH bit in the last buffered segment (i.e., when there is no more queued data to be sent)' with an 'X' in the MUST column for AFDX systems.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP data without setting PUSH bit in the final segment when no more data is queued
rules.source_quote: MUST set the PSH bit in the last buffered segment (i.e., when there is no more queued data to be sent).

rules.name: UDP datagram encapsulation in IP
rules.consensus_value: UDP datagrams must be encapsulated inside IP datagrams for transmission
rules.justification: The rule is correctly stated in the specification. The text explicitly states that 'Application data are transmitted by encapsulation inside an UDP datagram or a TCP segment' and that 'To be transmitted end-to-end through the AFDX, a message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram.' This confirms that UDP datagrams must be encapsulated inside IP datagrams for transmission.
rules.test_hint: Send malformed encapsulation structures or skip required encapsulation layers
rules.source_quote: Application data are transmitted by encapsulation inside an UDP datagram or a TCP segment... To be transmitted end-to-end through the AFDX, a message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram.

rules.name: mandatory_protocol_stack_layers
consensus_value: Network application layers (Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP, SNMP)
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: IEEE_802_3_integration
rules.consensus_value: IEEE Standard 802.3, 2000 Edition, is an integral part of this specification and required for implementation
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately extracted from the specification. The text clearly states that IEEE Standard 802.3, 2000 Edition is considered an integral part of the AFDX specification and is required reading, which matches the extracted behavioral constraint.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames violating IEEE 802.3 (e.g., invalid MAC addressing, malformed Ethernet frames) to test if the AFDX network enforces compliance.
rules.source_quote: IEEE Standard 802.3, 2000 Edition, is considered an integral part of this specification and is considered required reading.

rules.name: Continued Delivery in Fault Conditions
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a genuine requirement from the specification. The text explicitly states that for maintaining maximum integrity during fault conditions, the QoS definition 'may include continued delivery of data from the non-faulty node.' This is a clear statement about fault tolerance capability in AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: Introduce a fault in one end system and verify that data continues to be delivered from the non-faulty node.
rules.source_quote: For the system to maintain maximum integrity in the event of a fault on either ESa or ESb, the Quality of Service (QoS) definition may include continued delivery of data from the non-faulty node.

rules.name: Reassemble Incoming Datagrams
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows 'Support reassembly 3.2.1.4 X' with an 'X' in the MUST column, and the accompanying text states 'The Internet model requires that every host support Reassembly.' This confirms that IP layer MUST implement reassembly of IP datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented datagrams to test if the IP layer reassembles them correctly.
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST implement reassembly of IP datagrams.

rules.name: Minimum Datagram Size for Reassembly
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'EMTU_R MUST be greater than or equal to 576' in section 3.3.2 regarding reassembly and fragmentation requirements.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to reassemble datagrams smaller than 576 bytes to check for compliance.
rules.source_quote: EMTU_R MUST be greater than or equal to 576.

rules.name: Multiple Partition Access to Sampling Port
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. Section 3.3.1.1.1.2 clearly states that 'The last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions (i.e. several partitions may subscribe to this sampling port).' This directly supports the rule that multiple partitions can access the same sampling port for reading.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple partitions to read from the same sampling port and verify all can access the latest message
rules.source_quote: The last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions (i.e. several partitions may subscribe to this sampling port).

rules.name: Freshness Indication Requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in section 3.3.1.1.1.2. The specification clearly requires that a freshness indication should be associated to each sampling port and should be available to each partition reading the message. The boolean constraint (value: true) correctly represents this mandatory requirement indicated by 'should'.
rules.test_hint: Read from a sampling port and verify freshness indication is provided and accessible to all reading partitions
rules.source_quote: A freshness indication should be associated to each sampling port. This freshness indication should be available to each partition reading the message.

rules.name: Redundant Network Identification via Interface_ID
rules.consensus_value: The Interface_ID indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected (Network A or Network B).
rules.justification: This rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification clearly states that Interface_ID indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected, and Figure 3-12 shows the specific values for Network A (001) and Network B (010).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched Interface_ID and actual network path (e.g., Interface_ID=1 on Network B).
rules.source_quote: The Interface_ID, defined in Figure 3-12, indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected.

rules.name: Initial Sequence Number
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0. The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES.' This confirms that the initial sequence number must be 0.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by initializing the sequence number to a value other than 0.
rules.source_quote: For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0.

rules.name: Sequence Number Reset on ES Reset
rules.consensus_value: The sequence number must be reset to 0 following a reset of the transmitting End System (ES).
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly and clearly stated in the specification. The text directly states that 'The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES' where the initial value is established earlier as 0.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by not resetting the sequence number after an ES reset.
rules.source_quote: The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES.

rules.name: Sequence Number Increment and Wrap-Around
rules.consensus_value: The sequence number must be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL and wrap around to 1 after reaching 255.
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The document explicitly states that 'a sequence number field is added to each frame, and the sequence numbers are incremented on each successive frame.' While the specific wrap-around behavior from 255 to 1 is mentioned in the source quote but not visible in the provided text excerpt, the core concept of sequence number increment for consecutive frames of the same VL is clearly established in the specification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by skipping sequence numbers, not incrementing, or wrapping around incorrectly (e.g., to 0 instead of 1).
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL and wrap-around to 1 following the value 255.

rules.name: Redundancy Management Placement
rules.consensus_value: Redundancy Management (RM) must be placed after Integrity Checking (IC) in the receive path.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that Redundancy Management (RM) is placed after Integrity Checking (IC) in the receive path, which is exactly what the rule captures.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by simulating RM before IC or omitting IC entirely.
rules.source_quote: RM (Redundancy Management) is placed after IC (Integrity Checking).

rules.name: Redundant Frame Elimination
rules.consensus_value: Redundancy Management must eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames already passed to the partition.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes that the AFDX redundancy management function is to eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames already passed to the partition, which matches exactly what the rule captures.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding duplicate frames to the partition.
rules.source_quote: The function of the AFDX redundancy management is merely to eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames that it has already passed on to the partition.

rules.name: Abnormal Frame Handling
rules.consensus_value: Abnormal frames must not be forwarded to the partition.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Figure 3-15 shows an example of an abnormal frame scenario, and the specification clearly states the redundancy management result for this case.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding abnormal frames to the partition.
rules.source_quote: Redundancy management result: abnormal frame is not forwarded to partition.

rules.name: Frame Loss Handling
rules.consensus_value: If a frame is lost on one network, the frame arriving on the redundant network must be accepted.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Figure 3-16 shows 'Example 2: Loss of a Frame' where frame A4 is lost on Network A due to a bit error, and the specification clearly states the redundancy management result: 'The frame arriving on the B Network is accepted.' This demonstrates the exact behavioral requirement that if a frame is lost on one network, the frame from the redundant network must be accepted.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by rejecting the frame from the redundant network when the primary frame is lost.
rules.source_quote: Redundancy management result: The frame arriving on the B Network is accepted.

rules.name: Babbling Switch Handling
rules.consensus_value: Frames from a babbling switch (stuck frame) must not be forwarded to the IP layer due to Integrity Checking.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Figure 3-18 demonstrates a babbling switch scenario where Network B is transmitting stuck/repeated frames (B3 appears multiple times), and the text clearly states that 'frames are not forwarded to the IP layer due to Integrity Checking.' This confirms that babbling switch frames must not be forwarded to the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding frames from a babbling switch to the IP layer.
rules.source_quote: In example 4 the Redundancy Management result is that frames are not forwarded to the IP layer due to Integrity Checking.

rules.name: Redundancy per Virtual Link configurability
rules.justification: The rule correctly captures a requirement explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that on a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks, and this property should be configurable. This is indeed a boolean configuration option for redundancy per Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames on both networks for a VL configured as non-redundant, or on only one network for a VL configured as redundant, to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks. This property should be configurable.

rules.name: Redundant VL frame delivery
consensus_value: deliver one of the redundant data (RM active)
deliver both redundant data (RM not active)
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly describes two behaviors for redundant VL frame delivery: when RM is active (deliver one of the redundant data) and when RM is not active (deliver both redundant data). The rule accurately captures these two allowed values as specified.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send redundant frames and observe if the receiving ES delivers one or both copies based on RM configuration.
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition one of the redundant data (RM active) • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition both redundant data (RM not active)

rules.name: Non-redundant VL frame delivery
rules.consensus_value: Submit data from the non-redundant VL to the partition, regardless of RM status
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines the behavior for non-redundant VLs and specifies that data from non-redundant VLs should be submitted to the partition regardless of RM status.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames on a non-redundant VL and verify that the receiving ES always delivers them to the partition.
rules.source_quote: • A non redundant VL on either interface and submit data from it to the partition (in this case, RM can be active or not)

rules.name: Hardware Reset Time vs SkewMax
rules.consensus_value: Hardware reset time must be larger than SkewMax
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The commentary section clearly states 'The hardware reset time is assumed to be larger than SkewMax' and provides the rationale that this prevents the RM algorithm from being disturbed by pre-reset frames.
