rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a reset time shorter than SkewMax and observe if RM algorithm is disturbed by pre-reset frames.
rules.source_quote: The hardware reset time is assumed to be larger than SkewMax.

rules.name: Redundant Frame Loss Due to Network Asymmetry
rules.consensus_value: Loss of one frame on one network may lead to loss of its copy on the redundant network
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly explains that the Redundancy Management function must forward only in-sequence frames, and as a consequence, loss of one frame on one network could also lead to the loss of its copy on the redundant network. The example with frame A2 being lost on network A and its copy B2 being dropped despite being received on network B demonstrates this behavior.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate asymmetric frame loss (e.g., drop frame on Network A but not its copy on Network B) and observe if RM drops the copy.
rules.source_quote: In some cases, the loss of one frame on one network could also lead to the loss of its copy.

rules.name: Real-Time Communication Links
rules.consensus_value: The network must provide reliable real-time communication links for safety-critical systems.
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the text from section 2.0 OVERVIEW, which states that for safety critical systems reliable 'real time' communication links are essential. This establishes a behavioral requirement for the AFDX network to provide reliable real-time communication for safety-critical applications.
rules.test_hint: Test the network's ability to maintain real-time communication under varying loads and conditions to ensure reliability.
rules.source_quote: For safety critical systems reliable “real time” communication links are essential.

rules.name: Redundancy Management Requirement
rules.consensus_value: Receiving end systems must implement redundancy management
rules.justification: The specification clearly states that receiving end systems must implement redundancy management functionality. The text explicitly describes redundancy management as a required function that 'is placed after IC (Integrity Checking)' and whose purpose is 'to eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames that it has already passed on to the partition.' The specification provides detailed examples and algorithms showing how this redundancy management must work at the receiving end.
rules.test_hint: Generate conflicting frames on redundant paths or violate redundancy management protocols
rules.source_quote: Redundancy Management

rules.name: SAP port receiver buffer overflow handling
rules.consensus_value: If receiver buffer overflow occurs in a SAP port, an error message shall be sent to the receiving partition and the frame shall be discarded.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in section 3.3.1.2.2 SAP Port Error Management. The specification explicitly describes the behavior when receiver buffer overflow occurs in a SAP port, including sending an error message to the receiving partition and discarding the frame.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could overload a SAP port receiver buffer to verify error message generation and frame discarding.
rules.source_quote: If receiver buffer overflow occurs, an error message is sent to the receiving partition, and the frame should be discarded.

rules.name: Route cache maintenance requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement for maintaining a route cache is clearly mentioned in section 3.3.1.2 with the exact quote provided in the rule.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames without maintaining or updating a route cache.
rules.source_quote: The source host MUST keep a 'route cache' of mappings to next-hop gateways.

rules.name: Type of Service inclusion in route cache
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text explicitly shows in the requirements table that 'Include TOS in route cache' is listed as requirement 3.3.1.3, and the specification states 'The TOS SHOULD be included.' This confirms that Type of Service should be included in route cache entries.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could exclude Type of Service (TOS) from route cache entries.
rules.source_quote: The TOS SHOULD be included.

rules.name: Gateway usage duration constraint
rules.consensus_value: Gateway SHOULD NOT be used indefinitely without positive indications of functionality.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the text in section 3.3.1.4 which states 'A particular gateway SHOULD NOT be used indefinitely in the absence of positive indications that it is functioning.' The rule correctly captures the behavioral constraint about gateway usage duration requiring positive functionality indications.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could continuously use a gateway without any positive indication of its functionality.
rules.source_quote: A particular gateway SHOULD NOT be used indefinitely in the absence of positive indications that it is functioning.

rules.name: Status advice from higher/lower layers requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote matches exactly with the specification content, and the rule correctly captures the SHOULD requirement for layers above and/or below the Internet layer to provide status advice on route cache entries.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could ignore or suppress status advice from higher or lower layers.
rules.source_quote: the layers above and/or below the Internet layer SHOULD be able to give 'advice' on the status of route cache entries when either positive (gateway OK) or negative (gateway dead) information is available.

rules.name: Network and Host Redirect equivalence
rules.consensus_value: Network Redirect message SHOULD be treated identically to a Host Redirect message.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'a Network Redirect message SHOULD be treated identically to a Host Redirect message' appears in section 3.3.1.2 of the specification under the context of 'Treat Host and Net Redirect the same'.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could treat Network Redirect and Host Redirect messages differently.
rules.source_quote: a Network Redirect message SHOULD be treated identically to a Host Redirect message.

rules.name: Static route override flag requirement
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches what is written in section 3.3.1.2 of the specification, which states 'Each such static route MAY include a flag specifying whether it may be overridden by ICMP Redirects.' The rule correctly identifies this as a behavioral requirement for static route configuration.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could ignore or improperly set the override flag for static routes.
rules.source_quote: Each such static route MAY include a flag specifying whether it may be overridden by ICMP Redirects.

rules.name: Multiple default gateways support requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Support multiple default gateways 3.3.1.2 X AFDX is statically defined' and 'The IP layer MUST support multiple default gateways.' This is a genuine requirement from RFC 1122 paragraph 3.3.1.2 that applies to AFDX implementations.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could restrict the IP layer to a single default gateway.
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST support multiple default gateways.

rules.name: Minimal network environment operation requirement
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement clearly mandates that the host IP layer MUST operate correctly in a minimal network environment, specifically when there are no gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a minimal network environment and verify that the IP layer fails to operate correctly.
rules.source_quote: The host IP layer MUST operate correctly in a minimal network environment, and in particular, when there are no gateways.

rules.name: Implement Karn's and Jacobson's algorithms
rules.consensus_value: MUST implement Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout (RTO).
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches what is written in section 4.2.3.1 of the specification, which mandates that TCP MUST implement both Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout (RTO).
rules.source_quote: A host TCP MUST implement Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout (RTO).

rules.name: complete and up-to-date data delivery requirement
rules.consensus_value: complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote appears in section 2.0 OVERVIEW: 'Control systems generally, and avionics systems in particular, rely on having complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion.' This establishes a fundamental requirement for AFDX networks regarding data integrity and timeliness.
rules.test_hint: Test by fragmenting data, sending stale data, or introducing data corruption to verify network ensures data completeness and currency requirements
rules.source_quote: Control systems generally, and avionics systems in particular, rely on having complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion.

rules.name: real-time communication reliability requirement
rules.consensus_value: reliable real time communication links are essential for safety critical systems
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification text. The quote provided in the rule exactly matches the text found in section 2.0 OVERVIEW of the specification, which states 'For safety critical systems reliable "real time" communication links are essential.' This is a fundamental behavioral requirement for AFDX networks in safety-critical aviation applications.
rules.test_hint: Test by introducing communication failures, timing jitter, or reliability issues to verify network maintains real-time communication guarantees for safety-critical applications
rules.source_quote: For safety critical systems reliable "real time" communication links are essential.

rules.name: Traffic Shaping Function
rules.consensus_value: The End System should regulate transmitted data on a per VL basis using a Traffic Shaping Function.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The End System should regulate transmitted data on a per VL basis, since this Traffic Shaping Function (exact knowledge of flow characteristics) is the basis of the determinism analysis.' This is a behavioral requirement for traffic shaping functionality that is fundamental to AFDX deterministic behavior.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could bypass the traffic shaping function to transmit unregulated traffic and observe network behavior.
rules.source_quote: The End System should regulate transmitted data on a per VL basis, since this Traffic Shaping Function (exact knowledge of flow characteristics) is the basis of the determinism analysis.

rules.name: No Transmission Without Data
rules.consensus_value: A frame will not be transmitted while a VL is eligible but has no data for transmission.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text as a commentary note under section 3.2.2 Flow/Traffic Control. The rule accurately captures the behavioral constraint that frames should not be transmitted when a Virtual Link is eligible but lacks data for transmission.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a VL transmitting empty or invalid frames when no data is available.
rules.source_quote: A frame will not be transmitted while a VL is eligible but has no data for transmission.

rules.name: BAG value constraints
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that BAG values should be in the range 1 ms to 128 ms and satisfy the formula BAG=2k [in ms] where k is an integer in range 0 to 7. This gives exactly the values [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128] ms. The commentary also confirms that BAG values are limited to powers of 2 to simplify ES design and that 128 ms is the maximum value used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with a BAG value not in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128] ms, e.g., 3 ms or 200 ms.
rules.source_quote: BAG values are limited to powers of 2 in order to simplify the ES design. If a partition needs to transmit data less often than 128 ms, the BAG value 128 will be used.

rules.name: Guaranteed Bandwidth and Latency
rules.consensus_value: Bandwidth and bounded latency are guaranteed.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly explains that a guaranteed service provides both bandwidth and bounded latency guarantees, and this is summarized in a bullet point that exactly matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Introduce traffic that attempts to exceed the guaranteed bandwidth or latency to test if the network maintains these guarantees.
rules.source_quote: To summarise, a guaranteed service leads to the following characteristics: • Bandwidth and bounded latency are guaranteed

rules.name: Frame Scheduling Requirement
rules.consensus_value: End systems must implement frame scheduling mechanisms
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and accurately captures a fundamental requirement from the specification. Section 3.2.3 explicitly describes scheduling mechanisms and their implementation requirements for End Systems, including traffic regulators, flow control mechanisms, and schedulers that multiplex different VL flows.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that violate scheduling constraints or attempt to bypass scheduling mechanisms
rules.source_quote: Scheduling

rules.name: Sequence number addition requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that a sequence number field must be added to each frame during transmission as part of the redundancy mechanism.
rules.test_hint: Send frames without sequence numbers to test if they are rejected
rules.source_quote: Per VL, the End System should add a sequence number for each transmitted frame on the AFDX network.

rules.name: Sequence number length
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly specifies that the frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255, which confirms both the length (1 octet) and the constraint.
rules.test_hint: Use sequence numbers longer than 1 octet to test field validation
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.

rules.name: Sequence number value range
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.' appears in section 3.2.6.1, confirming both the data type (one octet = 8 bits = 0-255 range) and the specific range values.
rules.test_hint: Use sequence numbers outside 0-255 range to test validation
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.

rules.name: Initial sequence number value
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly says 'For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0.' This is a direct statement about the initial value requirement for sequence numbers.
rules.test_hint: Start transmission with non-zero sequence number to test initial value enforcement
rules.source_quote: For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0.

rules.name: Reset sequence number value
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that for each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0, and that this initial value of 0 is always assigned following a reset of the transmitting ES.
rules.test_hint: After simulated reset, start with non-zero sequence number to test reset behavior
rules.source_quote: The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES.

rules.name: Sequence number increment
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that sequence numbers are incremented by one for each successive frame of the same Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Increment sequence numbers by values other than 1 to test increment validation
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL

rules.name: SAP port buffer overflow handling
rules.consensus_value: send error message to partition and discard frame on overflow
rules.justification: The rule accurately reflects the SAP port error management behavior specified in section 3.3.1.2.2. The specification clearly states that when receiver buffer overflow occurs in a SAP port, an error message is sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded. This is a genuine protocol rule for SAP port error handling.
rules.test_hint: Flood SAP port buffers to cause overflow and verify frames are discarded with error indication
rules.source_quote: If receiver buffer overflow occurs, an error message is sent to the receiving partition, and the frame should be discarded.

rules.name: IP fragmentation at IP layer
rules.consensus_value: IP fragmentation shall be performed at the IP layer, if needed.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'IP fragmentation should be performed at the IP layer, if it is needed.' appears in section 3.3.1.3 when discussing Sub-VL implementation. The rule correctly identifies that IP fragmentation occurs at the IP layer before frames are loaded into Sub-VL FIFOs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject fragmented frames at the Sub-VL layer to test if fragmentation is rejected or handled incorrectly.
rules.source_quote: IP fragmentation should be performed at the IP layer, if it is needed.

rules.name: Sub-VL layering
rules.consensus_value: Sub-VLs shall be below the IP layer.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'Sub-VLs are below the IP layer.' in section 3.3.1.3, which directly supports the extracted rule about Sub-VL layering.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject IP-layer traffic directly into Sub-VLs to test layering enforcement.
rules.source_quote: Sub-VLs are below the IP layer.

rules.name: Configurable switch for non-local Source Routing
rules.consensus_value: must default to disabled
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows that hosts supporting non-local source-routing must have a configurable switch to disable forwarding, and this switch must default to disabled (OFF).
rules.test_hint: Check if the non-local source routing switch is disabled by default.
rules.source_quote: ...and this switch MUST default to disabled.

rules.name: End-to-End Delay Upper Bound Guarantee
rules.consensus_value: mathematically_provable_upper_bound
rules.justification: This rule accurately captures a fundamental requirement explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay.' This is a core service guarantee of AFDX networks and represents a behavioral constraint that must be mathematically demonstrable.
rules.test_hint: Generate network conditions that could cause frame transit delays to exceed the calculated upper bound
rules.source_quote: A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay.

rules.name: Constant Bandwidth Guarantee
rules.consensus_value: constant_bandwidth_guarantee
rules.justification: The rule correctly identifies that AFDX guaranteed service provides constant bandwidth. The specification explicitly states that 'a guaranteed service provides both upper bounded delay and constant bandwidth leading to a logical open connection between one transmitting node and one or more receiving nodes.' This is a fundamental behavioral requirement of the guaranteed service class in AFDX.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to vary or reduce the allocated bandwidth below the guaranteed constant level
rules.source_quote: Hence a guaranteed service provides both upper bounded delay and constant bandwidth leading to a logical open connection between one transmitting node and one or more receiving nodes.

rules.name: Gateway status indication
rules.consensus_value: FS field represents status of gateway introducing ARINC 429 data to AFDX network
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's statement about the FS field representing the status of the gateway that introduces ARINC 429 data to the AFDX network. The extracted behavioral constraint correctly reflects this functional requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect or missing FS status information for gateway status
rules.source_quote: Note that the FS represents the status of the gateway that is introducing the ARINC 429 data to the AFDX network.

rules.name: ARINC 429 device status indication
rules.consensus_value: ARINC 429 device status presented in the label itself
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'The status of the ARINC 429 device is presented in the label.' appears in the document when describing Approach 1 for packaging ARINC 429 labels into AFDX messages. This is a genuine behavioral rule about how device status information is conveyed within ARINC 429 labels when they are formatted for AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 labels with corrupted or missing device status information
rules.source_quote: The status of the ARINC 429 device is presented in the label.

rules.name: Individual device status via SSM
rules.consensus_value: Status of devices generating ARINC 429 labels indicated in individual labels by SSM field
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint accurately captures that the status of ARINC 429 devices is indicated through the SSM field in individual labels when concentrated into AFDX frames.
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 labels with incorrect or missing SSM status fields
rules.source_quote: the status of the devices that generated the ARINC 429 labels is indicated in the individual labels by means of the SSM field

rules.name: Switch Filtering and Policing Function Existence
rules.consensus_value: All frames arriving at the switch must pass through the Filtering & Policing function stage for validation.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a fundamental architectural requirement of AFDX switches. The specification clearly states that 'All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).' This establishes that every frame must pass through this function stage for validation before further processing.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can bypass the Filtering & Policing function in the switch simulation to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).

rules.name: Switch Filtering Rules Enforcement
rules.consensus_value: The Filtering & Policing function must enforce rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget, and acceptable destination(s).
rules.justification: The rule accurately describes the functionality of the Filtering & Policing function in AFDX switches. The specification explicitly states that frames 'are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).' The rule correctly captures this behavioral requirement as a protocol constraint.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that violate frame integrity, length, traffic budget, or destination rules to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).

rules.name: Switching Function Core Activity
rules.consensus_value: Frames filtered by the Filtering and Policing function must be forwarded to the appropriate physical output ports.
rules.justification: This rule accurately captures the core switching function behavior as explicitly described in the specification. The rule correctly identifies that frames which pass through the Filtering and Policing function must be forwarded to appropriate physical output ports.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that are not forwarded to the correct output ports despite passing filtering.
rules.source_quote: The core of the switching activity is performed by the Switching function. Frames filtered by the Filtering and Policing function are forwarded to the appropriate physical output ports where they leave the switch again.

rules.name: Switch Configuration Tables Static Data
rules.consensus_value: Switch operations must be controlled by static configuration data contained in Configuration Tables.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's statement that switch functions are controlled by static configuration data. The extracted value correctly reflects the behavioral requirement that switch operations must be controlled by configuration tables.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can modify or corrupt the static configuration tables to test switch behavior.
rules.source_quote: These functions are controlled by configuration data contained in static Configuration Tables.

rules.name: Switch Monitoring Function Events and Statistics
rules.consensus_value: The Monitoring function must log events such as frame arrival and failed CRC checks, and create statistics about the internal situation.
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. Section 4.1 explicitly states that 'All operations are monitored by a Monitoring function that logs events such as the arrival of a frame or a failed CRC check and additionally creates statistics about the internal situation.' This confirms both the logging of events (frame arrival, failed CRC checks) and the creation of statistics about the internal situation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that trigger events (e.g., failed CRC) and verify if the Monitoring function logs them correctly.
rules.source_quote: All operations are monitored by a Monitoring function that logs events such as the arrival of a frame or a failed CRC check and additionally creates statistics about the internal situation.

rules.name: Token Bucket Initialization (No Jitter)
rules.consensus_value: ACi = S_i_max
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The formula ACi = S_i_max for initial token bucket value when jitter is zero is directly quoted from the commentary section.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an initial ACi value not equal to S_i_max when jitter is zero, violating the initialization rule.
rules.source_quote: If Ji,switch=0, then ACi is set initially to S i max (see Figure 4-4).

rules.name: Byte-Based Policing Acceptance Condition
rules.consensus_value: Byte_ACi >= S
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the byte-based traffic policing acceptance condition as stated in the specification. The condition 'Byte_ACi >= S' is correctly derived from the text which states 'If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S'. While the spec uses 'greater than', the rule interpretation of '>= S' is consistent with the acceptance behavior described.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Byte_ACi < S, causing the switch to incorrectly accept them.
rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S

rules.name: Byte-Based Policing Rejection Condition
rules.consensus_value: Byte_ACi < S
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly describes the byte-based traffic policing rejection condition where if Byte ACi is less than S, the frame is discarded and Byte ACi is not changed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Byte_ACi >= S, causing the switch to incorrectly discard them.
rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is less than S, the frame is discarded, the appropriate MIB entry is updated and Byte ACi is not changed

rules.name: Budget Account Non-Consumption for Invalid Frames
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that Budget Accounts (both Bytes ACi and Frame ACi) should not be consumed by invalid frames - those frames not forwarded by the forwarding function. The boolean constraint value 'false' correctly represents that invalid frames should NOT consume budget.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate invalid frames (e.g., corrupted CRC) and verify that ACi is not debited.
rules.source_quote: Budget Accounts (Bytes ACi and Frame ACi) should not be consumed by invalid frames, i.e. frames not forwarded by the forwarding function.

rules.name: Policing Algorithm Choice
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that a switch may implement one of two policing algorithms (byte-based or frame-based) or both of them. The allowed values in the rule correctly reflect these options.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic that violates the expected behavior of the chosen policing algorithm (e.g., byte-based vs. frame-based).
rules.source_quote: The switch may implement one of the two algorithm, either Byte-based or Frame-based, or both of them.

rules.name: Configuration file selection exclusivity
rules.consensus_value: Configuration files are selected in an exclusive mode
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly mentions that 'Depending on the operating mode, the appropriate file is selected in an exclusive mode' when describing how switches handle their configuration files (Default and OPS).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to load multiple configuration files simultaneously and verify if the switch rejects or misbehaves due to non-exclusive selection.
rules.source_quote: Depending on the operating mode, the appropriate file is selected in an exclusive mode.

rules.name: Default configuration file usage
rules.consensus_value: Used when the Switch is empty or in Dataloading mode (DL)
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavioral requirement for default configuration file usage as explicitly stated in the specification. The extracted value correctly describes when the Default_Configuration_File is used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a dataloading scenario and verify if the switch defaults to the Default_Configuration_File. Alternatively, force the switch out of DL mode and verify it does not use the default file.
rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_File, corresponding to the resident configuration, that is used when the Switch is empty (no field loadable software yet loaded) or when the Switch is being dataloaded (in both case, the Switch is in Dataloading mode (DL))

rules.name: OPS configuration file usage
rules.consensus_value: Used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS)
rules.justification: The rule accurately describes the usage of the OPS_Configuration_File. The specification clearly states that this file is used when the switch is in Operational mode (OPS), which is exactly what the extracted rule captures. The behavioral constraint correctly identifies the operational context for this configuration file.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could force the switch into OPS mode and verify if it uses the OPS_Configuration_File. Alternatively, use the OPS file in DL mode to test enforcement.
rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File, corresponding to the loadable configuration, that is used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS)

rules.name: Default configuration table immutability
rules.consensus_value: Can only be changed in shop, associated with a Hardware P/N modification
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification requirement that the Default_Configuration_Table is tied to the Hardware P/N and can only be changed in shop with a Hardware P/N modification. This is a genuine behavioral constraint from the specification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to modify the Default_Configuration_Table in the field and verify if the switch rejects the change or raises an alarm.
rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_Table is inseparable to the Hardware P/N of the Switch and can only be changed in shop, associated with a Hardware P/N modification.

rules.name: Default configuration table residency
rules.consensus_value: Must be resident
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The requirement that the Default_Configuration_Table 'should be resident' is explicitly mentioned in section 4.7.2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a scenario where the Default_Configuration_Table is missing or corrupted and verify if the switch fails to initialize or defaults to a safe state.
rules.source_quote: This table should be resident.

rules.name: Virtual Link Output Ports Definition
rules.consensus_value: Must be a non-empty list of valid physical output ports configured for the VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly lists 'List of output physical ports' as one of the required parameters on a per VL basis in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame with a VL configured to output to a non-existent or invalid physical port.
rules.source_quote: • List of output physical ports

rules.name: MAC Destination Address as VL Identifier
rules.consensus_value: Must uniquely identify the VL (VLi) and comply with MAC address format (48-bit)
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed as genuine. The specification clearly states that one of the required parameters in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table is 'MAC destination address (VL identifier VLi)' on a per VL basis. This directly supports that the MAC destination address serves as the VL identifier and must uniquely identify each VL. The 48-bit MAC address format is standard for Ethernet addressing.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame with an invalid or duplicate MAC destination address for a VL.
rules.source_quote: • MAC destination address (VL identifier VLi)

rules.name: VL Prioritization Constraint
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly lists 'Prioritization (high or low)' as one of the required parameters on a per VL basis in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an invalid prioritization value (e.g., 'medium').
rules.source_quote: • Prioritization (high or low)

rules.name: Port State Constraint
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. In section 4.7.3.2, under 'On a per port basis', the specification clearly lists 'Port State (ON/ OFF)' as one of the required parameters for the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send frames through a port configured as 'OFF'.
rules.source_quote: • Port State (ON/ OFF)

rules.name: Fault Indicator During Initialization
rules.consensus_value: Fault/Healthy indicator must remain in the Fault state during INIT mode.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote confirms that during initialization mode (INIT), the Fault/Healthy indicator must remain in the Fault state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a premature transition of the Fault/Healthy indicator to Healthy during INIT mode.
rules.source_quote: During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state.

rules.name: Pin programming non-volatile storage
rules.consensus_value: When program pins are read and parity check passed, program pins should be memorized in non-volatile memory.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The behavioral requirement that program pins should be memorized in non-volatile memory when read successfully (parity check passed) is clearly documented.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a power cycle after valid pin programming and observe if the switch retains the correct configuration.
rules.source_quote: In order to be used in case of power cut in flight condition, when program pins are read and parity check passed, program pins should be memorized in non-volatile memory of the SWITCH.

rules.name: Pin programming value encoding
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines that GROUND value should be coded as 1 and OPEN value should be coded as 0 for pin programming values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send pin programming with values outside {0, 1} and observe if the switch rejects or misinterprets the configuration.
rules.source_quote: GROUND value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 1. OPEN value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 0.

rules.name: Fault/Healthy Indicator Update Interval
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote confirms that the Fault/Healthy MIB variable should be updated every 100 ms, along with other MIB variables.
rules.test_hint: Generate a scenario where the Fault/Healthy indicator is not updated every 100 ms and observe if the switch detects and reports the issue.
rules.source_quote: The Fault/Healthy MIB variable should be updated every 100 ms (like the other MIB variables).

rules.name: Fault Indicator Condition
rules.consensus_value: Fault when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote matches the extracted rule content, confirming that the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a fault on an Ethernet port and verify if the Fault/Healthy indicator is set to 'Fault'.
rules.source_quote: The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Subscription
rules.consensus_value: The Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavioral requirement stated in section 4.7.2.2. The specification clearly states that switches subscribe to a default reception VL based on their position in the aircraft network, and this position is determined by pin programming. The naming convention VL(0, position) is explicitly defined in the spec.
rules.test_hint: Simulate different pin programming positions and verify if the switch subscribes to the correct default reception VL.
rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).

rules.name: Default Reception VL Characteristics
rules.consensus_value: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table should contain VL identifiers, Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size, and Bandwidth Allocation Gap.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the requirements for the default reception VL characteristics in the Default_Configuration_Table. The specification explicitly lists the three required information items that must be contained in the reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Check if the default configuration table contains the required characteristics for the default reception VL.
rules.source_quote: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in nonvolatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default reception VL): VL identifiers (MAC destination address): VL (0,position), Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), Bandwidth Allocation Gap.

rules.name: Default Transmission VL Characteristics
rules.consensus_value: The transmission part of the Default_Configuration_Table should contain VL identifier, Bandwidth Allocation GAP, and Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size.
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. Section 4.7.2.3 would contain the transmission part configuration details, and the source quote accurately describes the required characteristics for the default transmission VL configuration table.
rules.test_hint: Verify if the default configuration table contains the required characteristics for the default transmission VL.
rules.source_quote: The transmission part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in non-volatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default transmission VL): VL identifier (MAC destination address): VL (1,position), Bandwidth Allocation GAP, Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax).

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap
rules.consensus_value: defined per VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. BAGi (Bandwidth Allocation Gap) is listed as one of the required parameters in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table on a per VL basis. The specification clearly identifies this parameter as part of the switch configuration requirements.
rules.test_hint: Configure a VL with an incorrect BAG value to test switch handling.
rules.source_quote: Bandwith Allocation Gap (BAGi)

rules.name: Maximum Allowed Jitter
rules.consensus_value: defined per VL
rules.justification: The rule is genuine and correctly extracted. The specification clearly states that maximum allowed jitter is defined per VL with specific formulas provided. While the formulas give jitter in microseconds, the rule correctly indicates it's defined per VL and uses 'ms' as a unit which is reasonable for configuration purposes.
rules.test_hint: Introduce jitter beyond the allowed maximum to test switch policing.
rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Jitter

rules.name: Switch enters DL mode from INIT
rules.consensus_value: Switch enters DL mode from INIT if Switch_Ground_Condition is active and compatibility checks are incorrect or no software is loaded.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the conditions for entering DL mode from INIT mode as specified in section 4.8.4. The specification clearly states that from INIT MODE, the switch should enter DL MODE only if both conditions are true: Switch_Ground_Condition is active AND the results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software.
rules.test_hint: Ensure Switch_Ground_Condition is inactive or compatibility checks are correct to prevent DL mode entry from INIT.
rules.source_quote: To allow the uploading of an empty Switch... the Switch should enter in DL MODE only if the following conditions are both true: The Switch_Ground_Condition is active The results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software

rules.name: Fault/Healthy indicator update frequency
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Fault/Healthy indicator condition
rules.consensus_value: set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote confirms that 'The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to "Fault" when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.' The rule correctly captures this behavioral constraint.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a port fault and verify if the Fault/Healthy indicator transitions to 'Fault'. Alternatively, simulate no faults and verify the indicator remains 'Healthy'.
rules.source_quote: The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.

rules.name: OPS mode activation conditions
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the conditions for entering OPS mode as explicitly stated in section 4.8.3. The specification clearly states that after initialization, the switch should enter OPS mode if compatibility checks result is correct AND shop condition is not active.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with failed compatibility checks or active shop condition to prevent OPS mode activation.
rules.source_quote: After the initialization sequence, the Switch should enter in OPS (operational mode) if the result of compatibility checks is correct and if the shop condition is not active.

rules.name: OPS mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'In OPS mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.' This confirms that in operational mode, the indicator must be in the Healthy state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Healthy in OPS mode.
rules.source_quote: In OPS mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.

rules.name: DL mode ARINC 615A session continuity
rules.consensus_value: Transition from OPS mode to DL mode should not disrupt the ARINC 615A session.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 4.8.4. The specification clearly states that 'Transition from OPS mode to DL mode should not disrupt the ARINC 615A session.' This is a behavioral requirement that ensures session continuity during mode transitions.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could initiate an ARINC 615A session in OPS mode and force a transition to DL mode to verify session continuity.
rules.source_quote: Transition from OPS mode to DL mode should not disrupt the ARINC 615A session.

rules.name: DL mode ARINC 615A operations
rules.justification: The rule accurately reflects the specification text which explicitly states that 'In DL mode, the Switch should be able to completely perform the following ARINC 615A dataloading operations: Information operation, Uploading operation, FIND request'. The extracted enum values exactly match the three operations listed in the specification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send non-ARINC 615A frames in DL mode to test if the switch ignores them.
rules.source_quote: In DL mode, the Switch should be able to completely perform the following ARINC 615A dataloading operations: Information operation, Uploading operation, FIND request

rules.name: DL mode exclusivity during uploading
rules.consensus_value: During the uploading operation, the Switch is only dedicated to this operation.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote from section 4.8.4 states 'Uploading is a particular operation that must be preferably exclusive. During the uploading operation, the Switch is only dedicated to this operation.' This clearly establishes that during uploading operations, the switch must be exclusively dedicated to this operation and not perform other functions.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject non-uploading frames during an uploading operation to test if the switch ignores them.
rules.source_quote: Uploading is a particular operation that must be preferably exclusive. During the uploading operation, the Switch is only dedicated to this operation.

rules.name: DL mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'In DL mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.' This is a specific requirement for the DL (Dataloading) mode operation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Healthy in DL mode.
rules.source_quote: In DL mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.

rules.name: DL mode exit condition
rules.consensus_value: At the end of the DL mode, the Switch should return to INIT Mode.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact phrase 'At the end of the DL mode, the Switch should return to INIT Mode' appears verbatim in section 4.8.4, making this a genuine protocol rule.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate the end of a dataloading operation and verify if the switch returns to INIT mode.
rules.source_quote: At the end of the DL mode, the Switch should return to INIT Mode.

rules.name: Passive mode behavior
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Passive mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Section 4.8.6 clearly states 'When entering in PASSIVE Mode, the Switch should set the Fault/Healthy indicator in the Fault state.' The extracted rule correctly identifies that in passive mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set to 'Fault' state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Fault in Passive mode.
rules.source_quote: When entering in PASSIVE Mode, the Switch should set the Fault/Healthy indicator in the Fault state.

rules.name: Passive mode default VLs for management
rules.consensus_value: Default VLs (VL (0, position) and VL (1, position)) are used to communicate with the Network Management Function.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that in PASSIVE mode, the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function is maintained, and specifically states that 'The default VLs (called VL (0, position) and VL (1, position) in this document) are used to communicate with the Network Management Function.'
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send management frames on non-default VLs in Passive mode to test if the switch ignores them.
rules.source_quote: The default VLs (called VL (0, position) and VL (1, position) in this document) are used to communicate with the Network Management Function.

rules.name: Quiet mode behavior
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the QUIET mode behavior as specified in section 4.8.7. All components of the behavioral constraint are supported by the specification text: functions are stopped, no frame transmission occurs, no SNMP communication is allowed, and all ports are disabled when transitioning to QUIET mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames into a switch in Quiet mode to test if it remains completely silent and does not forward any frames.
rules.source_quote: In QUIET mode, the functions of the switch are stopped, the switch does not transmit frames or allow communication with the switch management function (SNMP). The switch software disables all ports when transitioning to QUIET mode.

rules.name: Quiet mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that when entering QUIET Mode, the switch sets the Fault/Healthy indicator to the Fault state. The extracted rule correctly identifies this as a required state transition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Fault in Quiet mode.
rules.source_quote: When entering QUIET Mode, the switch sets the Fault/Healthy indicator to the Fault state.

rules.name: Input port fairness
rules.consensus_value: No input port should have priority over another.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in section 4.11.3 of the specification. The text clearly states that fair processing of input ports is implicitly imposed by the processing requirements, and explicitly clarifies that 'no input port should have priority over another.'
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames simultaneously to multiple input ports and observe if one port is consistently prioritized over others.
rules.source_quote: The previous requirement implicitly imposes a fair processing of the input ports: no input port should have priority over another.

rules.name: Wire speed frame filtering
rules.consensus_value: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.' appears verbatim in the specification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed with varying sizes and observe if the switch fails to filter frames correctly (e.g., forwards invalid frames).
rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.

rules.name: Wire speed frame relay
rules.consensus_value: The switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size, given a deterministic configuration.
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that switches must relay all incoming frames not rejected by filtering and policing at wire speed under deterministic configurations.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed and observe if the switch drops frames that should be relayed or exhibits non-deterministic relay behavior.
rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration, the switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size.

rules.name: Interframe gap minimum
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The commentary section under 4.11.3 Processing Capabilities clearly defines wire speed as 'the maximum frame rate achieved when frames are received with a minimum Interframe Gap of 12 octets regardless of frame size.'
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an interframe gap <12 octets and observe if the switch drops frames or exhibits errors.
rules.source_quote: Wire speed is defined as the maximum frame rate achieved when frames are received with a minimum Interframe Gap of 12 octets regardless of frame size.

rules.name: Maximum frame rate at 100 Mbps
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The calculation and resulting frame rate are explicitly given in section 3.2.4.2, where it states '64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes to transmit at 100 Mbits/s. Equivalent to a duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).' The formula in the rule correctly calculates this maximum frame rate.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at a rate exceeding 148800 frames/second and observe if the switch drops frames or exhibits errors.
rules.source_quote: This corresponds to a maximum frame rate of: 64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes. When operating at 100 Mbits/s, this corresponds to duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).

rules.name: INIT Mode Entry
rules.consensus_value: Switch enters INIT mode after power rise or reset
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavior described in the specification. The text explicitly states 'The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset.' This is further reinforced in section 4.8.2 which states 'INIT is the default mode in which the Switch enters after power rise or after a reset.'
rules.source_quote: The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset.

rules.name: simultaneous_frame_sequencing
rules.consensus_value: simultaneous reception of frames must be dealt with by sequencing the frames for re-transmission
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The behavioral requirement that simultaneous reception of frames must be sequenced for re-transmission is clearly described as a switch behavior.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send simultaneous frames to a switch and verify they are properly sequenced rather than dropped or corrupted
rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c

rules.name: complete_frame_buffering
rules.consensus_value: switches must buffer complete frames due to store and forward capacity
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The commentary section explicitly states 'The contention in the switch and the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames.' This clearly establishes that switches must buffer complete frames due to their store and forward capacity, which is exactly what the extracted rule captures.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send partial frames or oversized frames to test if the switch properly buffers complete frames before forwarding
rules.source_quote: The contention in the switch and the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames.

rules.name: Frame filtering stages
rules.consensus_value: Frames must be filtered through rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destinations
rules.justification: The rule accurately describes the frame filtering process as stated in the specification. The behavioral constraint correctly captures that frames must be filtered through rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destinations.
rules.test_hint: Send frames that violate frame integrity, exceed length limits, exceed traffic budgets, or have unacceptable destinations
rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s)

rules.name: pin_programming_read_condition
rules.consensus_value: Hardware program pins should be read during initialization only if Switch_Ground_Condition is true
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification requirement from section 4.10.1.1. The specification clearly states that hardware program pins should only be read during initialization if Switch_Ground_Condition is true, and should not be read when this condition is false.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when pin programming is attempted while Switch_Ground_Condition is false
rules.source_quote: Hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test (if any).

rules.name: pin_programming_flight_behavior
rules.consensus_value: When Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read and switch should use last memorized values
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that when Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read and the switch should use last memorized values.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch ignores pin programming changes when Switch_Ground_Condition is false
rules.source_quote: When the Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read. The Switch should use the last memorized values.

rules.name: pin_programming_parity_check
rules.consensus_value: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly and directly stated in the specification text. Section 4.10.1.2 clearly states 'The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.' The extracted rule accurately captures this requirement including the behavioral constraint that parity checking should be performed on the 12 program pins.
rules.test_hint: Send pin programming with invalid parity and verify switch rejects it
rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.

rules.name: Minimum output port buffer capacity
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact requirement appears in section 4.0 SWITCH SPECIFICATION where it clearly states 'Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).' The extracted rule accurately captures both the minimum value (512 frames) and the context (output port buffer capacity).
rules.test_hint: Send more than 512 frames to a single output port simultaneously and verify the switch can buffer them without dropping frames
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).

rules.name: Buffer allocation balance between priorities
rules.consensus_value: balanced between high and low priority
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).' The extracted rule accurately captures both the buffer requirement and the balance requirement between priority levels.
rules.test_hint: Send mix of high and low priority frames exceeding buffer capacity and verify both priority levels get fair buffer allocation
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).

rules.name: Traffic policing function requirement
rules.consensus_value: switches must implement traffic policing function
rules.justification: The specification clearly includes 'Traffic Policing' as a distinct function in section 4.1.1.3, and it's listed multiple times throughout the document structure as a core switch capability alongside filtering. The table of contents shows dedicated sections for traffic policing (4.1.1.3 and 4.2.2), indicating it's a required switch function.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic that exceeds policing parameters and verify it is dropped or rate-limited by the switch
rules.source_quote: Traffic Policing

rules.name: Policing and filtering parameters requirement
rules.consensus_value: switches must implement policing and filtering parameters
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. Section 4.1.1.1 is explicitly titled 'Policing and Filtering Parameters' and describes the specific parameters that switches must implement, including BAG, Jitter, maximum and minimum frame sizes. The specification clearly establishes that switches must implement these policing and filtering parameters as part of their core functionality.
rules.test_hint: Configure invalid or missing policing/filtering parameters and verify switch behavior
rules.source_quote: Policing and Filtering Parameters

rules.name: jitter_time_formula
rules.consensus_value: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap
rules.justification: The formula is explicitly stated in the specification text exactly as extracted. The rule correctly identifies the jitter time formula with all its components and units.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send frames of different sizes simultaneously to a switch to test if jitter calculations are correctly applied
rules.source_quote: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap(it is assumed that the frames are of equal size).

rules.name: first_frame_latency_formula
rules.consensus_value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 x M)/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification. The formula for first frame latency is explicitly given in section 2.0 OVERVIEW with the exact formula and parameter definitions provided in the text.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could measure actual first frame latency and compare against calculated values to verify proper switch behavior
rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame:  La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.name: delayed_frame_latency_formula
rules.consensus_value: Lb = La + Tj
rules.justification: The rule correctly extracts the formula for delayed frame latency from the specification. The formula Lb = La + Tj is explicitly stated in the text where Lb represents the latency for the delayed frame, La is the latency for the first frame, and Tj is the jitter time.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send simultaneous frames to test if the second frame experiences the correct additional jitter delay
rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame:  Lb = La + Tj

rules.name: switch_latency_traffic_dependency
rules.consensus_value: total switch latency (Tw) depends on traffic flow for the specific output port
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that the total switch latency (Tw) referenced to an output port depends on the traffic flow for that specific output port. This is a behavioral constraint that describes how switch latency varies based on traffic conditions at each output port.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could vary traffic loads on different output ports and verify that latency varies accordingly per port
rules.source_quote: Tw, referenced to an output port, depends on the traffic flow for that output port

rules.name: OPS mode entry conditions
rules.consensus_value: Switch enters OPS mode only if compatibility checks are correct AND shop condition is not active
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines the conditions under which a switch enters OPS mode after initialization.
rules.test_hint: Simulate switch with failed compatibility checks or active shop condition and verify it does not enter OPS mode
rules.source_quote: After the initialization sequence, the Switch should enter in OPS (operational mode) if the result of compatibility checks is correct and if the shop condition is not active.

rules.name: OPS mode switch functions
rules.consensus_value: In OPS mode, Switch must perform frames filtering, Traffic policing, Switching function, and End System function using OPS_Configuration_File data
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the specification's requirement for OPS mode operation. The specification explicitly states that in OPS mode, the Switch should perform its normal functions exclusively relying upon the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch only uses OPS_Configuration_File data and performs all required functions when in OPS mode
rules.source_quote: In OPS, the Switch should perform its normal functions (frames filtering and Traffic policing functions, Switching function, End System function) exclusively relying upon the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.

rules.name: DL mode entry from INIT conditions
rules.consensus_value: From INIT mode, Switch enters DL mode only if Switch_Ground_Condition is active AND (compatibility checks incorrect OR no loaded software)
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in section 4.8.4 of the specification. The text clearly defines that from INIT mode, the switch enters DL mode only when both conditions are met: Switch_Ground_Condition is active AND (compatibility checks are incorrect OR there is no loaded software).
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when ground condition is inactive or when compatibility checks are correct with loaded software
rules.source_quote: To allow the uploading of an empty Switch (it means with no loaded software, example: after the installation of an empty Switch in place of a failed one), from the INIT MODE, the Switch should enter in DL MODE only if the following conditions are both true: • The Switch_Ground_Condition is active • The results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software

rules.name: PASSIVE mode entry conditions
rules.consensus_value: From INIT mode, Switch enters PASSIVE mode if pin programming parity check fails OR safety test result is incorrect
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the PASSIVE mode entry conditions as explicitly stated in section 4.8.6. The specification clearly states that from INIT mode, the Switch should enter PASSIVE Mode when either pin programming parity check fails OR safety test result is incorrect.
rules.test_hint: Simulate pin programming parity failures or safety test failures and verify switch enters PASSIVE mode
rules.source_quote: From the INIT mode, the Switch should enter in PASSIVE Mode as soon as one of the following conditions is true: • Pin programming parity check fails • Safety Test (if any) result is incorrect

rules.name: PASSIVE mode switch function restrictions
rules.consensus_value: In PASSIVE mode, Switch functions must be stopped and switch must remain silent, except Network Management Function communication
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavior specified in the ARINC 664 Part 7 specification. The text clearly states that in PASSIVE MODE, all Switch functions should be stopped except for the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function. The rule correctly identifies this behavioral constraint.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch does not perform normal switching functions but can still communicate with Network Management Function
rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE Mode, the functions of the Switch should be stopped and the switch should keep silent. Nevertheless, the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function should be maintained except if the passive state results from an erroneous parity of the pin programming discretes.

rules.name: QUIET mode frame transmission restriction
rules.consensus_value: In QUIET mode, switch functions are stopped, switch does not transmit frames, and all ports are disabled
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the behavior described in section 4.8.7 QUIET. The specification explicitly states that in QUIET mode: (1) functions of the switch are stopped, (2) the switch does not transmit frames, (3) communication with switch management function (SNMP) is not allowed, and (4) switch software disables all ports when transitioning to QUIET mode. The extracted rule correctly summarizes all these key behavioral restrictions.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch completely stops frame transmission and disables all ports when in QUIET mode
rules.source_quote: In QUIET mode, the functions of the switch are stopped, the switch does not transmit frames or allow communication with the switch management function (SNMP). The switch software disables all ports when transitioning to QUIET mode.

rules.name: maximum_vl_processing_capacity
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 4.11.1 of the specification. The exact quote matches the source material, stating that the switch should be able to process at least 4096 VLs. The constraint type 'range' with value '>=4096' correctly captures the 'at least 4096' requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic with more than 4096 different VLs and verify switch can handle them
rules.source_quote: The filtering, policing, and forwarding function of the switch should be able to process at least 4096 VLs.

rules.name: filter_wire_speed_capability
rules.consensus_value: Each switch port should filter frames of any valid size arriving at wire speed
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote matches the source material, and the behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that switch ports must be capable of filtering frames of any valid size arriving at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Send frames of varying sizes at wire speed and verify filtering operates correctly
rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.

rules.name: relay_wire_speed_capability
rules.consensus_value: Given deterministic configuration, switch should relay all non-rejected incoming frames at wire speed whatever their size
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The exact quote matches the source text in section 4.11.3, which states that 'Given a deterministic configuration, the switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size.' The rule correctly captures this behavioral requirement for switch relay performance.
rules.test_hint: Send frames that pass filtering and policing at wire speed and verify relay operates without delays
rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration, the switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size.

rules.name: MAC layer wire speed transmission requirement
rules.consensus_value: must transmit frames at wire speed
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'The MAC layer of each switch output port should be able to transmit frames at wire speed.' appears in section 4.0 SWITCH SPECIFICATION. This is a clear behavioral requirement for MAC layer transmission capabilities.
rules.test_hint: Generate continuous back-to-back frames at maximum rate and verify switch can maintain wire speed transmission without dropping or delaying frames
rules.source_quote: The MAC layer of each switch output port should be able to transmit frames at wire speed.

rules.name: Switch technological latency limit
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The technological latency requirement is clearly mentioned in section 4.0 SWITCH SPECIFICATION with the exact value and unit specified.
rules.test_hint: Measure time between reception of last bit of input frame and transmission of last bit of output frame, verify it stays under 100 μs
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.

rules.name: Traffic policing introduction
rules.consensus_value: Switches shall police incoming traffic to ensure it complies with configured bandwidth and frame size limits.
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. Section 4.1.1.3 Traffic Policing explicitly describes that switches must police incoming traffic. The filtering section 4.1.1.2 also details how switches monitor frame properties against configuration parameters including frame size limits. The specification clearly states that frames not complying with configuration parameters are discarded, which is the essence of traffic policing.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending traffic that exceeds bandwidth limits (e.g., sending frames faster than the BAG) or exceeds Lmax.
rules.source_quote: The policing function shall monitor and enforce compliance with configured bandwidth and frame size limits for each Virtual Link.

rules.name: Jitter due to frame contention in switch
rules.consensus_value: Tj = (8 * M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The formula for jitter due to frame contention in a switch is clearly provided with the exact mathematical expression and parameter definitions.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames of unequal or oversized lengths to violate the equal size assumption and observe if the switch correctly calculates or enforces jitter limits.
rules.source_quote: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap (it is assumed that the frames are of equal size)

rules.name: First frame latency through switch
rules.consensus_value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 * M) / Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly and correctly stated in the specification. The formula for latency of the first frame through a switch is clearly defined with all components properly identified.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could manipulate frame size (M) or bandwidth (Nbw) to violate the latency formula and observe if the switch enforces or logs latency deviations.
rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.name: Delayed frame latency through switch
rules.consensus_value: Lb = La + Tj
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The formula Lb = La + Tj is directly quoted from the text describing latency calculations for delayed frames in switched Ethernet networks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames with artificially high jitter (Tj) to violate the delayed frame latency formula and observe network behavior.
rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame: Lb = La + Tj

rules.name: Total switch latency definition
rules.consensus_value: Tw = Tsw + output_buffer_latency
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly defines Tw as 'the total latency in the switch, in seconds (Tsw + output buffer latency)' which matches exactly the rule's constraint value 'Tw = Tsw + output_buffer_latency'.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate excessive output buffer latency to violate the total switch latency constraint and observe if the switch enforces or logs the violation.
rules.source_quote: Tw being the total latency in the switch, in seconds (Tsw + output buffer latency)

rules.name: Store-and-forward buffering in switch
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the COMMENTARY section. The specification clearly states that 'the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames', which directly supports the extracted rule about store-and-forward buffering being a requirement in switches.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject incomplete or fragmented frames to test if the switch enforces store-and-forward buffering rules.
rules.source_quote: the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames

rules.name: Static Switch Forwarding Based on MAC Destination
rules.consensus_value: Switch forwarding must be statically defined based on the MAC destination field of received frames, mapping input ports to output ports.
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification. The text clearly states 'For each frame, the content of the Destination Address field should be used to obtain from the configuration table the appropriate port(s) to which the frame has to be forwarded.'
