This describes static switch forwarding based on MAC destination address using a configuration table that maps destinations to output ports.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect or undefined MAC destination addresses to test switch forwarding logic.
rules.source_quote: Table 3-2 – Switch Forwarding: Input port, MAC destination field of the received frames, Output ports.

rules.name: Frame discard on link failure
rules.consensus_value: Frames held in buffers for a failed port must be discarded.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the requirement that frames held in buffers for a failed port must be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a link failure and verify if the switch discards frames queued for the failed port.
rules.source_quote: In the case of a link failure of a port, frames forwarded to and held in buffers of this port should be discarded for this port.

rules.name: High priority frame precedence
rules.consensus_value: High priority frames must be sent before low priority frames on the same output port.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The extracted rule correctly captures the behavioral requirement that high priority frames must be sent before low priority frames on the same output port.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send interleaved high and low priority frames and verify if the switch transmits high priority frames first.
rules.source_quote: For each output port, frames with a priority set to high should be sent prior to the one set to low.

rules.name: Non-preemption of low priority frames
rules.consensus_value: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted must not be pre-empted by a high priority frame.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint matches exactly with the specification requirement about non-preemption of low priority frames during transmission.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a low priority frame followed by a high priority frame during transmission and verify if the switch completes the low priority frame before transmitting the high priority one.
rules.source_quote: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted should not be pre-empted by the arrival of a high priority frame.

rules.name: Filtering and Forwarding Configuration
rules.consensus_value: In Operational mode (OPS), the filtering and forwarding functions must rely on the parameters contained in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table corresponding to the switch's current position.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in section 4.7.3.2 of the specification. The extracted rule accurately captures the behavioral requirement that in Operational mode (OPS), the filtering and forwarding functions must rely on parameters from the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table corresponding to the switch's current position.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that violate filtering or forwarding rules (e.g., incorrect VL identifiers, unauthorized MAC addresses) and observe if the switch enforces the rules (e.g., discards or misroutes frames).
rules.source_quote: In Operational mode (OPS), the filtering and forwarding functions rely on the parameters contained in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table, corresponding to the current position of the Switch.

rules.name: Frame Sequencing in Switch
rules.consensus_value: Frames are sequenced for re-transmission with a maximum jitter dependent on message length.
rules.justification: This rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text explicitly describes how switches handle simultaneous frame reception by sequencing them for re-transmission, and provides the exact formula for calculating the maximum jitter dependent on message length: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap. The behavioral description in the rule accurately captures this switching behavior.
rules.test_hint: Send frames simultaneously from different sources and verify that the switch sequences them correctly with the expected jitter.
rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c, with a maximum jitter dependent on the message length

rules.name: Maximum ACK Delay
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. Under the 'GENERATING ACKNOWLEDGMENTS' section, there is a clear entry for 'Delay less than 0.5 seconds 4.2.3.2 X' with the requirement 'The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.' This directly matches the extracted rule's constraint and source quote.
rules.test_hint: Configure delayed ACK with delay exceeding 0.5 seconds
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.

rules.name: Minimum ACK Frequency for Full Segments
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'In a stream of full-sized segments there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment.' appears in section 4.2.3.2, confirming that TCP should acknowledge at least every second full-size segment.
rules.test_hint: Send stream of full-size segments with ACK frequency less than every second segment
rules.source_quote: In a stream of full-sized segments there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment.

rules.name: Sender must generate checksum
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Sender compute checksum 4.2.2.7 X' followed by 'The sender MUST generate.' This directly confirms that the sender must generate the TCP checksum.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with missing or zero checksums to test sender compliance
rules.source_quote: The sender MUST generate.

rules.name: Receiver must check checksum
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The table clearly shows 'Receiver check checksum 4.2.2.7 X' with the requirement 'The receiver MUST check it.' This directly corresponds to the extracted rule requiring TCP checksum validation by the receiver.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with incorrect checksums to verify receiver rejects them
rules.source_quote: The receiver MUST check it.

rules.name: Use clock-driven ISN selection
rules.consensus_value: must use specified clock-driven selection
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The table clearly shows 'Use clock-driven ISN selection (Note 3) 4.2.2.9 X' with the requirement 'A TCP MUST use the specified clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers.' This matches exactly with the extracted rule's source quote and requirement.
rules.test_hint: Analyze ISN patterns across connections to verify proper clock-driven randomization
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST use the specified clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers.

rules.name: simultaneous_open_support
rules.consensus_value: TCP must support simultaneous open attempts
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement appears in section 4.2.2.10 under 'OPENING CONNECTIONS' with the exact statement 'A TCP MUST support simultaneous open attempts.' This is a clear behavioral requirement for TCP implementations.
rules.test_hint: Send simultaneous SYN packets from both ends and verify the connection establishes correctly
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST support simultaneous open attempts.

rules.name: syn_rcvd_state_tracking
rules.consensus_value: TCP implementation must keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN_RCVD state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement is clearly documented in section 4.2.2.11 under 'OPENING CONNECTIONS' with the exact wording matching the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Test different sequences of active/passive opens and verify state tracking is maintained correctly
rules.source_quote: TCP implementation MUST keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN_RCVD state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN.

rules.name: passive_open_isolation
rules.consensus_value: Every passive OPEN call must not affect any previously created connection record
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the specification text found in section 4.2.2.18, which states 'Every passive OPEN call it MUST NOT affect any previously created connection record.' This is a clear behavioral requirement that passive OPEN calls must maintain isolation from existing connections.
rules.test_hint: Create multiple passive opens on same port and verify existing connections remain unaffected
rules.source_quote: Every passive OPEN call it MUST NOT affect any previously created connection record.

rules.name: reject_broadcast_multicast_open
rules.consensus_value: TCP implementation must reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address)
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement that TCP must reject local OPEN calls to invalid remote IP addresses (including broadcast or multicast addresses) is clearly documented with the exact wording provided in the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to open TCP connection to broadcast or multicast address and verify it is rejected
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).

rules.name: discard_syn_to_broadcast_multicast
rules.consensus_value: TCP implementation must silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.' in section 4.2.3.10. The extracted rule accurately captures this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send SYN segment to broadcast/multicast address and verify it is silently discarded
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.

rules.name: inform_application_of_aborted_connection
rules.consensus_value: If a TCP connection is closed by the remote site, the local application must be informed whether it closed normally or was aborted
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The requirement is clearly documented in section 4.2.2.13 of the TCP requirements summary, mandating that applications must be informed whether a remote connection closure was normal or aborted.
rules.test_hint: Close connection remotely with RST vs FIN and verify application receives correct close indication
rules.source_quote: If a TCP connection is closed by the remote site, the local application MUST be informed whether it closed normally or was aborted.

rules.name: time_wait_duration
rules.consensus_value: 2 * MSL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.' The extracted rule correctly identifies this as a formula constraint '2 * MSL' which matches the specification requirement.
rules.test_hint: Close connection actively and verify it remains in TIME-WAIT for exactly 2*MSL seconds
rules.source_quote: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.

rules.name: ACK Aggregation Required
rules.consensus_value: must_aggregate_acks
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'In general, the processing of received segments MUST be implemented to aggregate ACK segments whenever possible' appears in section 4.2.2.20 under the 'GENERATING ACKNOWLEDGMENTS' section. This is a clear behavioral requirement that TCP implementations must aggregate ACK segments when possible.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple segments that could be aggregated and verify ACK behavior
rules.source_quote: In general, the processing of received segments MUST be implemented to aggregate ACK segments whenever possible.

rules.name: Receiver SWS Avoidance Required
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly shows 'Receiver SWS-Avoidance algorithm (Note 4) 4.2.3.3 X' with the requirement 'A TCP MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the receiver.' This is a mandatory requirement (MUST) that applies to AFDX implementations.
rules.test_hint: Test receiver behavior with small window updates to verify SWS avoidance
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the receiver.

rules.name: Invalid remote IP address rejection
rules.consensus_value: must_reject_invalid_remote_ip
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).' This directly matches the extracted rule about rejecting invalid remote IP addresses.
rules.test_hint: Attempt TCP connection to invalid IP addresses and verify the connection is rejected
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.

rules.name: Invalid source address SYN rejection
rules.consensus_value: must_ignore_syn_with_invalid_source
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. Section 4.2.3.10 contains the exact requirement about rejecting SYN packets with invalid source addresses.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP SYN packets with invalid source IP addresses and verify they are ignored
rules.source_quote: An incoming SYN with an invalid source address must be ignored either by TCP or by the IP layer.

rules.name: Broadcast/multicast SYN silently discarded
rules.consensus_value: must_silently_discard_broadcast_multicast_syn
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.' appears in section 4.2.3.10 of the requirements table.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP SYN packets to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify they are silently discarded without any response
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.

rules.name: Urgent pointer points to last octet
rules.consensus_value: points to sequence number of last octet, not last+1
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The table clearly shows under 'URGENT DATA' section that 'Pointer points to last octet' with reference 4.2.2.4 and includes the exact quote provided in the rule.
rules.test_hint: Send urgent data with pointer incorrectly pointing to LAST+1 instead of LAST octet
rules.source_quote: The urgent pointer points to the sequence number of the LAST octet (not LAST+1)

rules.name: Support arbitrary length urgent data
rules.consensus_value: must support urgent data sequence of any length
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The exact quote 'A TCP MUST support a sequence of urgent data of any length.' appears in section 4.2.2.4 under the URGENT DATA section. The extracted rule accurately captures this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Send extremely long urgent data sequences to test length handling limits
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST support a sequence of urgent data of any length.

rules.name: Ignore unsupported options
rules.consensus_value: must ignore without error any unimplemented option with length field
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The extracted rule accurately captures both the requirement and the quoted text from section 4.2.2.5.
rules.test_hint: Send segments with unrecognized TCP options to verify they are silently ignored
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST ignore without error any TCP option it does not implement, assuming that the option has a length field.

rules.name: Default MSS value
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement is found in section 4.2.2.6 under TCP OPTIONS, which clearly states 'If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.' The extracted value of 536 bytes is correct.
rules.test_hint: Establish connections without MSS option and verify 536-byte MSS is assumed
rules.source_quote: If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.

rules.name: Initial Round Trip Time
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Under section 4.2.3.1 'Recommended initial values and bounds', the text clearly states '(a) RTT = 0 seconds.' as one of the values that SHOULD be used to initialize the estimation parameters for a new connection.
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP connection with non-zero initial RTT value
rules.source_quote: RTT = 0 seconds.

rules.name: Initial Retransmission Timeout
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Under section 4.2.3.1 'Recommended initial values and bounds', it clearly states '(b) RTO = 3 seconds.' as a recommended initial value for the retransmission timeout.
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP connection with different initial RTO value
rules.source_quote: RTO = 3 seconds.

rules.name: Maximum Retransmission Timeout Upper Bound
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that 'the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds' for the RTO (Retransmission Timeout). The rule correctly captures both the numerical value (240 seconds) and the context (upper bound for RTO).
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP with RTO upper bound exceeding 240 seconds
rules.source_quote: the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.

rules.name: Minimum R1 Retransmission Threshold
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'The value of R1 SHOULD correspond to at least 3 retransmissions, at the current RTO.' This confirms both the field name (R1), the constraint type (minimum threshold), and the specific value (3 retransmissions).
rules.test_hint: Configure R1 threshold below 3 retransmissions
rules.source_quote: The value of R1 SHOULD correspond to at least 3 retransmissions, at the current RTO.

rules.name: Minimum SYN R2 Threshold
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes.' This translates to a minimum threshold of 180 seconds as correctly extracted.
rules.test_hint: Configure SYN R2 threshold below 180 seconds (3 minutes)
rules.source_quote: R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes.

rules.name: Flexible Bandwidth Usage for Virtual Link
rules.consensus_value: A VL may use less bandwidth by increasing the frame interval or reducing frame size at any time.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a behavioral specification from the AFDX standard. The specification explicitly states that a VL may use less bandwidth by increasing frame interval or reducing frame size, which is exactly what this rule describes. This is a legitimate operational characteristic of Virtual Links in AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test network resilience by dynamically varying frame intervals or sizes within a VL, but this is not a violation. Violations would involve exceeding Lmax or T_GAP.
rules.source_quote: The VL may use less bandwidth through an increased frame interval or smaller frames at any time.

rules.name: BAG Enforcement
rules.consensus_value: The frame flow is regulated to guarantee the BAG for each VL. The traffic regulator should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds.
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text. The source quote accurately reflects the specification's requirement that 'To guarantee the BAG for each VL the frame flow is regulated' and the behavioral constraint about traffic regulation to ensure no more than one frame per BAG interval is consistent with the BAG definition and flow regulation described in the spec.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could transmit multiple frames within a single BAG interval to test BAG enforcement.
rules.source_quote: To guarantee the BAG for each VL the frame flow is regulated as shown in Figure 3-5. On a per VL basis the traffic regulator (traffic shaping function) should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds.

rules.name: Jitter Definition
rules.consensus_value: 0 < Jitter < MaxBAG
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The formula '0 < Jitter < MaxBAG' appears directly in the text within section 3.2.3 discussing traffic shaping function. The constraint correctly captures that jitter must be greater than 0 and less than the maximum BAG value.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce jitter values outside the allowed range (e.g., 0 ms, equal to or exceeding BAG) to test jitter bounds.
rules.source_quote: 0 < Jitter < MaxBAG

rules.name: Maximum Usable Bandwidth
rules.consensus_value: maximum_usable_bandwidth = Lmax / BAG
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The formula, units, and explanation are all correctly extracted from the source text.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic exceeding the calculated maximum bandwidth (Lmax/BAG) to test bandwidth enforcement.
rules.source_quote: The maximum usable bandwidth of each VL is characterised by its BAG and its authorized Lmax (maximum VL frame size). The maximum usable bandwidth = Lmax / BAG in Kbytes per seconds.

rules.name: Maximum Latency Calculation
rules.consensus_value: Maximum latency is calculable.
rules.justification: This rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly explains that in AFDX networks with bounded arrival distribution and exact bandwidth regulated traffic control, 'This results in a calculable maximum latency in the network, rather than a probabilistic latency.' This is contrasted with typical Ethernet networks that have probabilistic latency. The rule correctly captures this fundamental characteristic of AFDX.
rules.source_quote: This results in a calculable maximum latency in the network, rather than a probabilistic latency.

rules.name: Maximum frame delay enforcement
rules.consensus_value: discard_frames_exceeding_max_delay
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'An output port should not transmit frames that are older than "max delay." The "max delay" parameter is defined on a per port basis in the configuration table.' This is a behavioral requirement that frames exceeding the configured max delay parameter should be discarded, which matches the extracted rule perfectly.
rules.test_hint: Delay frames in switch buffers beyond configured max_delay parameter and verify they are discarded
rules.source_quote: An output port should not transmit frames that are older than "max delay." The "max delay" parameter is defined on a per port basis in the configuration table.

rules.name: Window size unsigned treatment
rules.consensus_value: must be treated as unsigned number
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly and directly stated in the specification text. The exact requirement 'The window size MUST be treated as an unsigned number' appears in section 4.2.2.3 of the specification table.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with window size values that would be negative if interpreted as signed but positive as unsigned
rules.source_quote: The window size MUST be treated as an unsigned number.

rules.name: No window shrinking from right
rules.consensus_value: receiver should not move right window edge to the left
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote and behavioral constraint accurately reflect the requirement that a TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window by moving the right window edge to the left.
rules.test_hint: Generate sequence where receiver shrinks window by moving right edge leftward and observe if network handles this violation
rules.source_quote: A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left.

rules.name: Sender robust against window shrinking
rules.consensus_value: must be robust against window shrinking that makes useable window negative
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The exact quote matches what is provided in the rule, and it clearly establishes that a sending TCP MUST be robust against window shrinking that may cause the useable window to become negative.
rules.test_hint: Force window shrinking that creates negative useable window and verify sender handles it gracefully
rules.source_quote: However, a sending TCP MUST be robust against window shrinking, which may cause "useable window" (see Section 4.2.3.4) to become negative

rules.name: Zero window probing support required
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The table clearly shows 'Sender probe zero window 4.2.2.17 X' with an 'X' in the MUST column, and the comment section states 'Probing of zero (offered) windows MUST be supported.' This directly supports the extracted rule requiring zero window probing support.
rules.test_hint: Create zero window condition and verify that sender generates window probe packets
rules.source_quote: Probing of zero (offered) windows MUST be supported.

rules.name: First zero window probe timing
rules.consensus_value: first probe should be sent after retransmission timeout period
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text clearly states 'The transmitting host SHOULD send the first zero-window probe when a zero window has existed for the retransmission timeout period.' This matches exactly with the extracted rule's behavioral constraint that 'first probe should be sent after retransmission timeout period'.
rules.test_hint: Set zero window and measure timing of first probe relative to RTO to verify compliance
rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD send the first zero-window probe when a zero window has existed for the retransmission timeout period.

rules.name: Exponential backoff for zero window probes
rules.consensus_value: exponentially increase interval between successive probes
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. Section 4.2.2.17 clearly states 'The transmitting host SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes.' in the context of zero window probing.
rules.test_hint: Monitor multiple zero window probe intervals to verify exponential backoff pattern
rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes.

rules.name: Bandwidth Limitation per Virtual Link
rules.consensus_value: Transmission of frames on a Virtual Link must be delayed according to the BAG_i to comply with bandwidth limitations.
rules.justification: The rule correctly captures the traffic shaping behavior described in the specification. The text explicitly states 'The transmission will be delayed according to the bandwidth limitation of the VL (traffic shaping)' and shows formulas where BAG_i is used to calculate maximum latency, indicating that frame transmission must respect BAG intervals to enforce bandwidth limitations.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames violating BAG_i by sending them faster than the allowed interval.
rules.source_quote: The transmission will be delayed according to the bandwidth limitation of the VL (traffic shaping).

rules.name: Frame-based traffic policing
rules.consensus_value: Frame-based policing filters VL traffic based on bandwidth usage expressed in frames per second
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The document explicitly describes frame-based traffic policing as filtering VL traffic based on bandwidth usage expressed in frames per second, which matches the extracted rule exactly.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by exceeding the frame rate limit (frames per second) for a VL configured with frame-based policing.
rules.source_quote: The frame-based traffic policing filters out the VL in terms of bandwidth usage expressed in frames per second

rules.name: Use VL identifier to access filtering and policing parameters
rules.consensus_value: must be used to obtain filtering and policing parameters from the configuration table
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'The switch should use the VL identifier to obtain the appropriate information of filtering and policing from the configuration table.' This is a clear behavioral requirement that the VL identifier must be used to access filtering and policing parameters.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with a VL ID not present in the configuration table and verify policing behavior.
rules.source_quote: The switch should use the VL identifier to obtain the appropriate information of filtering and policing from the configuration table.

rules.name: Support one-to-one or one-to-many MAC destination to account mapping
consensus_value: one ACi for one MAC destination address (VLi)
one ACi for a group of MAC destination addresses (VLs)
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in section 4.2.2 Traffic Policing. The specification clearly describes two types of relationships between MAC destination address and ACi that should be supported, matching exactly what the extracted rule captures.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can test both mapping types by generating frames with MAC addresses configured for one-to-one or one-to-many relationships.
rules.source_quote: Two types of relationship between MAC destination address and ACi should be supported: • One ACi for only one MAC destination address (VLi) • One ACi for a group (several) of MAC destination addresses (VLs): Account Sharing

rules.name: Shared VL must belong to only one account
rules.consensus_value: must be part of one and only one account
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'A shared VL will be part of one and only one account' directly confirms this behavioral requirement.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with a VL ID configured to belong to multiple accounts and verify policing behavior.
rules.source_quote: A shared VL will be part of one and only one account.

rules.name: One BAG, jitter, and maximum size value per VL
rules.consensus_value: one BAG value per VL, one jitter value per VL, and one maximum size value per VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact phrase 'There should be one BAG value per VL, one jitter value per VL, and one maximum size value per VL.' appears verbatim in the specification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with inconsistent BAG, jitter, or size values for the same VL and verify policing behavior.
rules.source_quote: There should be one BAG value per VL, one jitter value per VL, and one maximum size value per VL.

rules.name: Maximum Allowed Jitter Constraint
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. In section 4.7.3.2 Filtering_Policing and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table, the specification clearly lists 'Maximum allowed Jitter' as one of the required parameters on a per VL basis. The rule correctly identifies this as a traffic policing parameter related to jitter control, though the specification doesn't explicitly state the unit or range constraints.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with jitter exceeding the configured maximum allowed jitter for the VL.
rules.source_quote: • Maximum allowed Jitter

rules.name: Accounting Mode Constraint
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text explicitly states 'ACcount (ACi) [specifying if this account is shared or not]' which indicates that ACi is an enumerated field with two possible values: shared or not shared.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an invalid accounting mode (e.g., neither 'shared' nor 'not_shared').
rules.source_quote: • ACcount (ACi) [specifying if this account is shared or not]

rules.name: Exact Bandwidth Regulated Traffic Control
rules.consensus_value: bounded_arrival_distribution
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly establishes that AFDX networks use bounded arrival distribution which implies exact bandwidth regulated traffic control, distinguishing it from typical Ethernet networks that use random/Poisson arrival distributions.
rules.test_hint: Generate frame arrivals that violate bounded arrival distribution patterns, such as burst traffic exceeding bandwidth limits
rules.source_quote: frame delivery follows a bounded arrival distribution. This bounded arrival implies exact bandwidth regulated traffic control.

rules.name: Ethernet frame size must meet Virtual Link minimum for byte-based policing
rules.consensus_value: S >= Smin
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. In section 4.1.1.2 Frame Filtering, it clearly lists as one of the frame filtering criteria: 'Ethernet frame size (S) greater than or equal to Smin, only in case where byte-based traffic policing is used'. The extracted rule correctly captures this constraint as S >= Smin and correctly identifies that it only applies when byte-based traffic policing is used.
rules.test_hint: When byte-based policing is enabled, send frames smaller than Smin for the Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (S) greater than or equal to Smin, only in case where byte-based traffic policing is used

rules.name: Initial AC account setting
rules.consensus_value: AC_i = S_i_max
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly indicates that initially, the ACcount for VLi (also called ACi, expressed in bytes) is set to S_i_max. The formula AC_i = S_i_max correctly captures this initialization requirement.
rules.source_quote: Initially, the ACcount for VLi (also called ACi, expressed in bytes) is set to

rules.name: AC account crediting rate limit
rules.consensus_value: upper_limit = BAG_i
rules.justification: The rule correctly captures that the AC account crediting has an upper limit of BAG_i as explicitly stated in the specification. The formula representation 'upper_limit = BAG_i' accurately reflects the constraint described in the text.
rules.source_quote: ACi is credited as time elapses, proportionally to S i max with an upper limit of BAG i

rules.name: Budget consumption exclusion for invalid frames
rules.consensus_value: no_budget_consumed_for_discarded_frames
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly and clearly stated in the specification text. The exact behavior described in the rule matches the specification requirement that budget accounts should not be consumed by invalid frames that are discarded by filtering mechanisms.
rules.test_hint: Send invalid frames that get discarded and verify budget accounts are not debited
rules.source_quote: Budget Accounts (Bytes ACi and Frame ACi) should not be consumed by invalid frames, i.e. frames not forwarded by the forwarding function. No budget should be consumed by frames that are discarded by the filtering mechanisms.

rules.name: Upper bound on RTO
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly states 'the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds' when discussing the recommended upper and lower bounds on the RTO.
rules.test_hint: Set RTO upper bound to a value greater than 240 seconds and observe behavior.
rules.source_quote: The upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.

rules.name: Nagle Algorithm
rules.justification: The rule is accurately extracted from the specification. The text clearly states 'A TCP SHOULD implement the Nagle Algorithm [TCP:9] to coalesce short segments.' This is marked as 'SHOULD' (not mandatory) in the requirements table, which aligns with the boolean constraint value of true indicating it should be implemented.
rules.test_hint: Disable Nagle Algorithm and send short segments to see if they are coalesced.
rules.source_quote: A TCP SHOULD implement the Nagle Algorithm [TCP:9] to coalesce short segments.

rules.name: Application Data Encapsulation
rules.consensus_value: Application data must be encapsulated inside a UDP datagram or a TCP segment for transmission.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the text in Appendix C - Network Terminology under 'Application Data' definition.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send application data without encapsulating it in a UDP datagram or TCP segment.
rules.source_quote: Application data are transmitted by encapsulation inside an UDP datagram or a TCP segment.

rules.name: Message Encapsulation
rules.consensus_value: A message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram for end-to-end transmission through the AFDX.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote exactly matches the text found in Appendix C - Network Terminology, which clearly defines that messages must be encapsulated inside IP datagrams for end-to-end transmission through AFDX.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send a message without encapsulating it in an IP datagram.
rules.source_quote: To be transmitted end-to-end through the AFDX, a message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram.

rules.name: IP Datagram Fragmentation
rules.consensus_value: If a UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it must be broken into fragments.
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The behavioral constraint accurately captures the fragmentation requirement described in the 'Fragment' definition in Appendix C.
rules.test_hint: Send a UDP datagram that exceeds the MTU without fragmenting it.
rules.source_quote: Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.

rules.name: IP Datagram Structure
rules.consensus_value: An IP datagram must consist of an IP header followed by transport layer data.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The extracted behavioral constraint accurately captures the structure requirement for IP datagrams as defined in the ARINC 664 Part 7 specification.
rules.test_hint: Construct an IP datagram without an IP header or without transport layer data.
rules.source_quote: An IP datagram consists of an IP header followed by transport layer data, i.e., of an IP header followed by an UDP datagram or a segment.

rules.name: Frame Structure
rules.consensus_value: A frame must consist of a MAC header followed by a packet.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification text. The definition of 'Frame' is clearly provided in Appendix C - Network Terminology.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame without a MAC header or without a packet.
rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet.

rules.name: BAG frame rate limiting
rules.consensus_value: max_one_frame_per_bag_interval
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The behavioral constraint 'max_one_frame_per_bag_interval' accurately captures the requirement that no more than one frame should be sent in each BAG interval for a given Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames within a single BAG interval on the same VL
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis the traffic regulator (traffic shaping function) should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds

rules.name: Single frame maximum latency constraint
rules.consensus_value: MAX_Latency_i ≤ BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The formula MAX_Latency_i ≤ BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission is explicitly provided for the first case where partitions transmit evenly spaced data with no bursts or fragmentation.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that arrive with latency exceeding BAG + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.source_quote: the total allowed latency for a given VLi is: MAX_Latency i ≤ BAG i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.name: Two traffic priority classes
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states 'The Switch should have a traffic prioritization mechanism based on MAC destination address with 2 traffic classes: High Priority and Low Priority.' This directly matches the extracted rule that specifies exactly two traffic classes with the names 'High Priority' and 'Low Priority'.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic with invalid priority levels or test priority handling with frames assigned to undefined classes
rules.source_quote: The Switch should have a traffic prioritization mechanism based on MAC destination address with 2 traffic classes: High Priority and Low Priority.

rules.name: High priority frame transmission precedence
rules.consensus_value: high_priority_before_low_priority
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The requirement for high priority frames to be sent before low priority frames is explicitly mentioned in the switching function section.
rules.test_hint: Queue low priority frames then send high priority frames to verify scheduling order
rules.source_quote: For each output port, frames with a priority set to high should be sent prior to the one set to low.

rules.name: No frame preemption during transmission
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted should not be pre-empted by the arrival of a high priority frame.' directly supports this rule. The boolean constraint value of 'false' correctly represents that frame preemption should NOT occur during transmission.
rules.test_hint: Start transmitting low priority frame then send high priority frame to verify no preemption occurs
rules.source_quote: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted should not be pre-empted by the arrival of a high priority frame.

rules.name: IANA assigned port number range
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification text. The document clearly defines three groups of transport layer port numbers managed by IANA, with assigned port numbers explicitly stated as '0 – 1023'.
rules.source_quote: Assigned port numbers: 0 – 1023

rules.name: IANA registered port number range
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly defines three groups of port numbers managed by IANA, and 'Registered port numbers: 1024 – 49151' is one of them.
rules.source_quote: Registered port numbers: 1024 – 49151

rules.name: Dynamic/Private port number range
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the Dynamic/Private port number range as explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines three groups of transport layer port numbers managed by IANA, with the third group being 'Dynamic/Private port numbers: 49152 – 65535'.
rules.source_quote: Dynamic/Private port numbers: 49152 – 65535

rules.name: Prohibition on shrinking window
rules.consensus_value: SHOULD NOT shrink the window (move right window edge left)
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The AFDX Transport Layer TCP Requirements Summary table shows 'Shrink window from right 4.2.2.16' with an 'X' in the 'MUST NOT' column, and the comments section clearly states 'A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left.' This matches exactly with the extracted rule's constraint value.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment that reduces the window size from a previously advertised value.
rules.source_quote: A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left.

rules.name: Default MSS value
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact quote 'If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.' appears in the document under section 4.2.2.6, confirming that the default MSS value is indeed 536 bytes when no MSS option is received.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could omit the MSS option in a SYN segment to test if the default 536 bytes is assumed.
rules.source_quote: If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.

rules.name: TIME-WAIT state duration
rules.consensus_value: 2 * MSL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The requirement clearly states that when a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL (2 times Maximum Segment Lifetime). The extracted rule accurately captures this requirement with the correct formula '2 * MSL'.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could close a connection and verify the TIME-WAIT state duration is exactly 2 times the Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL).
rules.source_quote: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.

rules.name: Initial RTO value
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under 'Recommended initial values and bounds 4.2.3.1'. The specification clearly states '(b) RTO = 3 seconds' as a recommended initial value for the retransmission timeout.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could initialize RTO to a value other than 3 seconds (e.g., 1 second or 10 seconds).
rules.source_quote: RTO = 3 seconds.

rules.name: RTO upper bound
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that 'the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds' for RTO (Retransmission Timeout). This is found in the TCP requirements section referencing RFC-1122 paragraph 4.2.3.1.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set the RTO upper bound to a value other than 240 seconds (e.g., 120 seconds or 300 seconds).
rules.source_quote: the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.

rules.name: Maximum ACK delay
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The document clearly shows under 'Delayed ACKs 4.2.3.2' section that 'The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.' This is a direct requirement from RFC-1122 section 4.2.3.2 regarding TCP acknowledgment delays.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could delay ACKs for >= 0.5 seconds (e.g., 0.6 seconds).
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.

rules.name: TTL default value in AFDX
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. In the table on page 108, under 'Configurable Time to Live 4.2.2.19', there is a clear comment stating 'Not used in AFDX, default value is 1'. This confirms that the TTL default value in AFDX is indeed 1.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set TTL to a value other than 1 (e.g., 64 or 255).
rules.source_quote: default value is 1

rules.name: Virtual Link as unidirectional logical communication path
rules.consensus_value: A Virtual Link (VL) is a unidirectional logical communication path from one source End System to one or more destination End Systems. It defines a multicast flow of AFDX frames.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the definition of Virtual Link from section 3.2.1. The specification explicitly states that 'A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems' and mentions it's a 'conceptual communication object' that represents a path. The rule correctly identifies this as a unidirectional logical communication path with multicast capability (one-to-many).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames from multiple source End Systems on the same VL or by sending bidirectional traffic on a VL.
rules.source_quote: Virtual Link: A Virtual Link (VL) is a unidirectional logical communication path from one source End System to one or more destination End Systems.

rules.name: Unidirectional Connection
rules.consensus_value: A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems.
rules.justification: This rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly defines that 'A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems' in section 3.2.1. This is a fundamental property of Virtual Links in AFDX.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate a VL with bidirectional traffic or multiple source end-systems to violate unidirectionality.
rules.source_quote: A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems, shown in Figure 3-2.

rules.name: Ordinal Integrity
rules.consensus_value: For each Virtual Link, the End System should maintain the ordering of data as delivered by a partition, for both transmission and reception.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly and directly stated in the specification text. The extracted constraint accurately captures the requirement for ordinal integrity on Virtual Links.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could reorder frames within a VL to test if ordinal integrity is enforced.
rules.source_quote: For each Virtual Link, the End System should maintain the ordering of data as delivered by a partition, for both transmission and reception (ordinal integrity).

rules.name: Source Partition Exclusivity
rules.consensus_value: One Virtual Link should not be shared by two or more source partitions.
rules.justification: This rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The exact phrase 'One Virtual Link should not be shared by two or more source partitions.' appears verbatim in the commentary section of 3.2.1, establishing that Virtual Links must be exclusive to a single source partition to maintain proper segregation between partitions at the network level.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate multiple partitions transmitting on the same VL to test exclusivity.
rules.source_quote: One Virtual Link should not be shared by two or more source partitions.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) definition
rules.consensus_value: BAGi represents the minimum interval between the start of consecutive frames for Virtual Link VLi (expressed in seconds)
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Jitter definition for Virtual Link
rules.consensus_value: Ji,switch represents the maximum jitter (window) within which a frame for VLi is assured to be located when entering a switch (expressed in seconds)
rules.justification: The rule is genuinely stated in the specification. The text clearly defines Ji,switch as 'The Jitter (representing the Window a frame is assured to be located within) associated to VLi entering a particular switch' and explicitly states it is 'expressed in seconds'. The extracted rule accurately captures this definition and constraint.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by introducing jitter exceeding Ji,switch for a given VL.
rules.source_quote: The Jitter (representing the Window a frame is assured to be located within) associated to VLi entering a particular switch is Ji,switch (expressed in seconds)

rules.name: Default Reception VL Identifier Format
rules.consensus_value: VL (0, position), where '0' indicates reception VL and 'position' depends on the switch's location in the aircraft network.
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the VL identifier format for default reception VLs as explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that switches subscribe to 'VL (0, position)' where '0' indicates reception VL and 'position' depends on the switch's location in the aircraft network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with malformed VL identifiers (e.g., VL (2, position), VL (0, invalid)) and observe if the switch rejects or processes them incorrectly.
rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position). '0' indicates that it is a reception VL.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Non-Volatile Configuration
rules.consensus_value: Must include VL identifier (MAC destination address), maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), and Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) in non-volatile memory.
rules.justification: The rule is directly and explicitly stated in the specification. Section 4.7.2.2 clearly lists the exact three requirements that must be contained in non-volatile memory for the default reception VL configuration: VL identifiers (MAC destination address), Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), and Bandwidth Allocation Gap.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with missing or corrupted default reception VL configuration parameters and observe if the switch fails to process them.
rules.source_quote: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in nonvolatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default reception VL): VL identifiers (MAC destination address): VL (0,position), Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), Bandwidth Allocation Gap.

rules.name: Default Transmission VL Identifier Bit Mapping
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures the pin programming specification for VL identifier bits P1 to P12. The specification clearly states that these bits correspond to pin programming values where '1 = GROUND and 0 = OPEN', which matches exactly with the extracted rule's constraint mapping.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with VL identifiers using invalid bit mappings (e.g., values other than 0 or 1 for P1-P12) and observe if the switch rejects or misinterprets them.
rules.source_quote: Where P1 to P12 correspond to the following pin programming values: 1 = GROUND and 0 = OPEN.

rules.name: UDP port unreachable message prohibition
rules.justification: This rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The table explicitly states that UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message for datagrams to ports with no pending LISTEN call, but AFDX marks this as 'NOT APPLICABLE' with the comment 'Only ICMP echo request and echo reply are allowed.' This effectively prohibits ICMP Port Unreachable messages in AFDX implementations.
rules.test_hint: Send UDP datagrams to non-listening ports and verify that ICMP Port Unreachable messages are not generated
rules.source_quote: If a datagram arrives addressed to a UDP port for which there is no pending LISTEN call, UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message. [AFDX: NOT APPLICABLE - Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.]

rules.name: Virtual Link Bandwidth and Frame Interval Bounds
rules.consensus_value: bounded_bandwidth_and_frame_interval
rules.justification: The rule accurately captures a fundamental requirement stated in the specification. The text explicitly states 'This is achieved by bounding both the bandwidth and the frame delivery interval for each VL.' This describes the exact behavioral constraint that Virtual Links must have bounded bandwidth and frame delivery intervals to maintain deterministic network properties.
rules.test_hint: Violate VL bandwidth bounds or send frames outside the defined frame delivery interval
rules.source_quote: This is achieved by bounding both the bandwidth and the frame delivery interval for each VL.

rules.name: Single source per VL constraint
rules.consensus_value: only_one_source_per_vl
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The text clearly states that only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL, which directly supports the extracted rule about single source per VL constraint.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with the same VL ID but from multiple different source end systems
rules.source_quote: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.

rules.name: Switch subscribes to unique default reception VL
rules.consensus_value: Each switch subscribes to exactly one unique reception VL based on position
rules.justification: The rule is directly stated in the specification. Section 4.7.2.2 explicitly states that 'Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).' The word 'unique' and 'one' confirm that each switch subscribes to exactly one reception VL based on its position.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when configured with multiple default reception VLs or no default reception VL
rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).

rules.name: Switch has unique default transmission VL
rules.consensus_value: Each switch has exactly one unique transmission VL based on position
rules.justification: The rule is correctly extracted from the specification. The text explicitly states that each switch has a unique default transmission VL based on its position, using the notation VL(1, position) where '1' indicates transmission and 'position' indicates the VL depends on the switch's position in the aircraft network.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when configured with multiple default transmission VLs
rules.source_quote: Each Switch has a unique default transmission VL, further called VL (1, position).

rules.name: Maximum allowed total Ethernet line size per VL
rules.consensus_value: configurable per VL
rules.justification: The specification clearly states that both default reception and transmission VL configurations must contain 'Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax)' as a configurable parameter. The rule correctly identifies this as Smax (capitalized in the rule but lowercase in spec - this is acceptable variation) and correctly notes it is configurable per VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL that exceed the configured Smax value to test policing function
rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)

rules.name: Minimum allowed total Ethernet line size per VL
rules.consensus_value: configurable per VL
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification. The Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table section clearly lists 'Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)' as a per-VL parameter that must be configured. This is indeed a configurable parameter for policing functions on a per-VL basis.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL that are smaller than the configured Smin value to test policing function
rules.source_quote: Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)

rules.name: VL priority classification
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. Under section 4.7.3.2 Filtering_Policing and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table, it clearly lists 'Prioritization (high or low)' as one of the parameters required on a per VL basis. This confirms that VL priority can only be classified as either 'high' or 'low'.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior by sending frames on VLs with different priority settings and verify scheduling/buffering behavior
rules.source_quote: Prioritization (high or low)
